objects.description: Standard vector of strings used here as a return type reference for search_paths(). This is a standard library type and not a custom type defined in this header; included only because it appears in the API surface. Its construction and management follow standard C++ rules.

Container class owning a list of use_type_base pointers for binding input parameters to SOCI statements. It extends std::vector<use_type_base*> and deletes stored elements in its destructor. Provides exchange() helpers to push constructed use bindings, supporting Boost.Fusion sequences and non-sequence types. Construction details of use_type_base/use_type_ptr/use_container are external to this header.

Container class owning a list of into_type_base pointers for binding output columns/values from SOCI statements. It extends std::vector<into_type_base*> and deletes stored elements in its destructor. Provides exchange() helpers to push constructed into bindings, supporting Boost.Fusion sequences and non-sequence types. Construction details of into_type_base/into_type_ptr/into_container are external to this header.

Template specialization of soci::details::into_type for soci::blob, deriving from standard_into_type. It adapts a blob for use as an INTO binding in SOCI statements, optionally with an indicator. Construction forwards the blob address and x_blob type tag to the base.

Template specialization of soci::details::use_type for soci::blob, deriving from standard_use_type. It adapts a blob for use as a USE binding in SOCI statements, supporting const and non-const blobs, optional indicator, and an optional named parameter. Internally forwards the blob pointer, x_blob tag, constness flag, and name to the base.

Template specialization of soci::details::exchange_traits for soci::blob. It declares the SOCI basic type family as basic_type_tag and sets the x_type discriminator to x_blob so the framework treats blobs as a basic exchange type.

objects.definition: class session;
objects.description: Forward declaration of soci::session representing a database session/connection. Only declared here; full definition is elsewhere. Used to construct/initialize blob instances.
Forward declaration of backend-specific BLOB implementation used by soci::blob. The actual definition is provided by database backends. Only declared here.

High-level SOCI BLOB wrapper managing a backend-specific blob handle. Provides initialization from a session or directly from a backend pointer, length querying, reading/writing from start with optional offset, appending, trimming, and access to the underlying backend. Non-copyable, movable. Correct usage requires calling initialize(session) or constructing with a session before I/O; otherwise ensure_initialized() will enforce validity. Destruction releases the owned backend via unique_ptr.

objects.definition: class session;
objects.description: Forward declaration of soci::session, representing a database session/connection. Only declared here; full definition is elsewhere. Used as a parameter in failover callbacks to allow replaying initialization on a new connection. Details unknown in this header.

Abstract callback interface for reporting and controlling failover events in soci. Users subclass this and override lifecycle hooks: started(), finished(session&), failed(bool& retry, std::string& newTarget), and aborted(). Default implementations are no-ops. The failed() method allows the handler to request another reconnect attempt and optionally provide a new target connection string.

Describes database column metadata within the soci namespace. Fields include the column name, deprecated logical data_type (type), the backend db_type (dataType), length (for text), precision, scale, and nullability. Used to carry schema information retrieved from databases.

Explicit specialization of soci::type_conversion for soci::column_info. Defines how to convert from soci::values to column_info, including helper get_numeric_value and from_base that populates column_info fields based on metadata in values. This is a complete definition in this header.

Owns parameters used to open a SOCI session. Holds a backend factory pointer or backend name reference, a connect string, and a map of option name/value pairs. Provides parsing from and building to a space-separated name=value string, option accessors, boolean option interpretation, and standard copy/move semantics. Construction requires either a backend factory, a backend name, or a full connection string. Destruction and move-reset behavior are defined in the implementation; no ownership transfer details are visible here. Unknown details: exact parsing rules and exception types are defined elsewhere.

objects.definition: class session;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a session class used by connection_pool. Its full definition is not present in this header, so details of its interface and lifecycle are unknown.

A non-copyable pool managing a fixed number of soci::session objects using a PIMPL implementation. Provides indexed access to a session, leasing APIs to acquire an available slot (blocking and timed try), and a method to return a leased slot. Construction requires a pool size; destruction releases all resources. The implementation type is hidden via pimpl_.

Base exception type for SOCI errors, derived from std::runtime_error. It stores an error message and optional layered context, provides full message via what(), and exposes classification via error_category along with optional backend-specific metadata (backend name, error code, SQLSTATE). It holds a private pointer to an internal extra info structure managed by the class implementation.

objects.definition:
enum error_category
    {
        connection_error,
        invalid_statement,
        no_privilege,
        no_data,
        constraint_violation,
        unknown_transaction_state,
        system_error,
        unknown
    };
objects.description: Enumeration defined inside soci::soci_error class that categorizes SOCI errors into common classes such as connection errors, invalid statements, privilege issues, no data, constraint violations, unknown transaction state, system errors, and unknown.

objects.definition: class soci_error_extra_info;
objects.description: Forward-declared internal helper class used by soci::soci_error to store optional extra information (e.g., context stack). The full definition is not present in this header and is likely provided in the library implementation.
Empty tag type used for dispatch indicating a built-in/basic SOCI exchange type.
Empty tag type used for dispatch indicating a user-defined SOCI exchange type (handled via type_conversion).
Specialization declaring SOCI signed 8-bit integer as a basic exchange type with x_type = x_int8.
Specialization for unsigned 8-bit integer; basic exchange type x_uint8.
Specialization for signed 16-bit integer; basic exchange type x_int16.
Specialization for unsigned 16-bit integer; basic exchange type x_uint16.
Specialization for signed 32-bit integer; basic exchange type x_int32.
Specialization for unsigned 32-bit integer; basic exchange type x_uint32.
Specialization for signed 64-bit integer; basic exchange type x_int64.
Specialization for unsigned 64-bit integer; basic exchange type x_uint64.

Specialization inheriting behavior from exchange_traits<soci_l_or_ll_int_t>. soci_l_or_ll_t is a type alias defined elsewhere for either long or long long; this trait maps it to the corresponding integer trait. Full meaning of soci_l_or_ll_int_t is declared outside this header.
Specialization inheriting behavior from exchange_traits<soci_ul_or_ull_int_t>. soci_ul_or_ull_t resolves to unsigned long or unsigned long long; underlying alias type is defined elsewhere.
Specialization for double-precision floating-point; basic exchange type x_double.
Specialization for single character; basic exchange type x_char.
Specialization for std::string; basic exchange type x_stdstring.
Specialization for std::wstring; basic exchange type x_stdwstring.
Specialization for std::tm time structure; basic exchange type x_stdtm.

Abstract base for all INTO bindings (output data) used by SOCI during statement execution/fetch. It defines the lifecycle hooks for binding output buffers and supports reporting/resizing element counts (resize is meaningful for vector-based INTOs).

Concrete INTO binding for single (non-vector) basic types. Holds a pointer to user data, its exchange_type, and optional indicator. Bridges to backend via standard_into_type_backend. Size is always 1. Provides a convert_from_base hook for user-defined conversions.

Concrete INTO binding for vectors of basic types. Manages a vector data buffer, optional parallel vector of indicators, and fetch window [begin_, *end_). Bridges to backend via vector_into_type_backend. Supports resizing and reporting size.

objects.definition: typedef type_ptr<into_type_base> into_type_ptr;
objects.description: Smart pointer/handle to into_type_base polymorphic objects created by helper factories. Exact semantics of type_ptr are defined in soci/type-ptr.h (not shown here).

objects.definition: class prepare_temp_type;
objects.description: Forward declaration of an internal helper type used during statement preparation. Definition not present in this header.

objects.definition: class standard_into_type_backend;
objects.description: Forward declaration of backend interface for single-value INTO bindings. Implemented by database backends. Definition not present here.

objects.definition: class vector_into_type_backend;
objects.description: Forward declaration of backend interface for vector INTO bindings. Implemented by database backends. Definition not present here.

objects.definition: class statement_impl;
objects.description: Forward declaration of the concrete statement implementation used internally by SOCI. Definition not present here.

objects.definition: class session;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a connection/session object representing a database session in SOCI. Definition not present here.

objects.definition: namespace soci { namespace details { typedef void no_indicator; } }
objects.description: Tag type used to indicate absence of an indicator with into(). It is a typedef alias of void, serving purely as a dispatch tag in templates.
Strongly-typed scoped enumeration indicating when logging should occur within the soci namespace. Values: never (disable logging), always (log unconditionally), on_error (log only on errors).
Simple POD-like struct storing a single bound SQL parameter: its name and value. Used by the logger to keep track of parameters for the current query.

Abstract base class for customizing SOCI logging. Derive from it and implement do_clone() and typically override start_query(); optionally override add/clear parameter and stream/query accessor methods. Holds the current query parameters in queryParams_. Non-copyable; use clone() for polymorphic copying.

Value-semantics wrapper owning a logger_impl. Ensures non-null implementation, manages lifetime (copies clone the impl, destructor deletes it), and forwards logging API calls. Acts as the public handle for logging.

Lightweight, copyable temporary object for executing a one-shot SQL statement with bound parameters in SOCI. It accumulates SQL fragments via operator<< and binds into/use elements via operator,. Manages an internal ref_counted_statement pointer and throws from destructor on failure (noexcept(false)).
Lightweight helper that stores a session pointer and starts a once_temp_type chain via operator<< to execute an immediate SQL statement. Acts as a factory for once_temp_type.

Lightweight helper holding a session pointer that begins a prepared-statement build chain via operator<<, returning a prepare_temp_type for further binding. Essentially a factory for prepare_temp_type.

User-facing DDL builder for constructing and executing SQL Data Definition Language statements against a session. Supports creating tables, adding/altering/dropping columns, constraints (unique, primary key, foreign key), appending arbitrary SQL, and setting a tail delimiter. Manages an internal ref_counted_statement and can throw from destructor (noexcept(false)). Deprecated overloads accept data_type and map to db_type.

Lightweight, copyable helper class used during statement preparation in SOCI. It accumulates SQL fragments and binds (into/use types and containers) into an underlying ref_counted_prepare_info. It holds a raw pointer to ref_counted_prepare_info, which manages the prepared statement metadata. Construction requires a soci::session. Copy/assign share the same underlying prepare info through reference counting (details in ref_counted_prepare_info, not defined here). Destruction releases the reference. Unknown details: ownership semantics and lifetime rules are governed by ref_counted_prepare_info; this header provides only the interface.

Reference-counted implementation class for stored procedures, derived from statement_impl. Manages its own lifetime via inc_ref/dec_ref and delegates execution/fetch to the base statement interface. Construction is supported from a session or from a prepared temporary object.

Public value-semantic handle for executing stored procedures. Holds a ref-counted pointer to details::procedure_impl and forwards execute/fetch. Constructible from details::prepare_temp_type. Copying shares the same implementation via intrusive reference counting. Users call execute() and optionally fetch(); got_data() reports if any rowset data was obtained.

Abstract base class defining a string-to-string SQL query transformation functor interface. Implementations override operator()(const std::string&) to return a transformed query. Used to plug user-defined transformations just before statement execution. Lifetime and ownership are not specified here; no virtual constructors are provided.

Reference-counted container for prepared statement metadata in SOCI. Holds SQL text (via base) and binds/defines to be used when constructing a statement_impl. Provides exchange() overloads to collect use/into bindings and a final_action() hook to complete preparation. Details of base class ref_counted_statement_base, vectors (into_type_vector/use_type_vector), and related types are declared elsewhere. Construction requires a soci::session reference. Destruction/ownership managed via reference counting inherited from ref_counted_statement_base. Unknown specifics of get_query() and final_action() implementation.

Abstract base class for reference-counted SOCI statements used by both once and prepared statement flows. Manages a manual reference count and triggers final_action() when count drops to zero, appending any accumulated tail SQL to the internal query stream beforehand. Holds a reference to a session, an output string stream (via get_query_stream()), a tail string used for portable DDL assembly, and a need_comma flag used while building SQL fragments. Construction requires a session&, destruction is virtual; copying is disabled. Note: ownership is self-managed via inc_ref()/dec_ref() and self-delete; use only through the provided ref counting protocol.

Concrete ref-counted statement that executes a SOCI statement upon final_action() when its reference count reaches zero (via base class dec_ref()). Wraps a soci::statement instance constructed from the provided session and forwards exchange(T&) to it for binding into/use elements. Intended as the vehicle for "once" statements; builds SQL via base accumulation/tail mechanisms and executes in final_action(). Copying is implicitly disabled via base. Lifecycle is managed by inc_ref()/dec_ref() with self-deletion in the base.

Full specialization of soci::details::into_type for soci::row enabling selection into a dynamic row. It adapts a row reference for use with statements: define() registers the row with the statement, post_fetch() resets the row get counter and optionally triggers conversion. This type is constructed directly by user code when binding a row to a statement. Copying is disabled. Ownership: holds a non-owning reference to a soci::row managed by the caller.
Full specialization of soci::details::exchange_traits for soci::row designating the exchange family as basic_type_tag. Used by SOCI type system to classify how row participates in data exchange.

Holds metadata for a single result-set column, including its name and database type. Provides getters/setters; data_type members are deprecated in favor of db_type. No ownership semantics beyond being stored by soci::row.

Container for a single database row used by SOCI. Holds column metadata, typed value holders, and indicators. Provides typed extraction via get()/move_as(), name/position lookup, and iteration-like access. Non-copyable, movable. Call clean_up() to release internal holders before reuse; add_properties() and add_holder() are used internally by SOCI backends to build the row.

Explicit specialization of soci::details::use_type for soci::rowid. It adapts a rowid value (by reference or const reference, optionally with an indicator) for use-binding in SOCI statements, forwarding to standard_use_type with the x_rowid data exchange type. It does not own the rowid; it wraps a pointer to an external instance.

Explicit specialization of soci::details::into_type for soci::rowid. It adapts a rowid lvalue (optionally with an indicator) for into-binding in SOCI statements, delegating to standard_into_type with the x_rowid exchange type. It references, but does not own, the provided rowid.
Explicit specialization of soci::details::exchange_traits for soci::rowid, classifying rowid as belonging to the basic_type_tag family so SOCI’s type dispatch knows how to exchange it.

Opaque handle representing a database ROWID for the SOCI library. It wraps a backend-specific row identifier via details::rowid_backend and is constructed from a soci::session. Ownership of the backend pointer is managed by rowid; lifetime is tied to the rowid instance. The header provides only the interface; construction attaches to a session; get_backend exposes the underlying backend pointer for internal use.

Database session class managing a connection to a SOCI backend. Provides connection lifecycle (open/close/reconnect), transaction control (begin/commit/rollback), SQL composition helpers (once/prepare/operator<< and query stream), logging, basic portable DDL/DML helpers, sequence/identity utilities, schema/column introspection helpers, and creation of backend-specific low-level objects. Moveable, non-copyable. Holds ownership of a backend session and optional connection pool association.
Enumeration of database column/value types exposed to users of SOCI. data_type is a deprecated legacy synonym with coarser granularity; db_type is the canonical type used by the API.

objects.definition:
// the enum type for indicator variables
enum indicator { i_ok, i_null, i_truncated };
objects.description: Indicator flags accompanying fetched/bound values: value present, NULL, or truncated.

objects.definition:
enum exchange_type
{
    x_char,
    x_stdstring,
    x_stdwstring,
    x_int8,
    x_uint8,
    x_int16,
    x_uint16,
    x_int32,
    x_uint32,
    x_int64,
    x_uint64,
    x_double,
    x_stdtm,
    x_statement,
    x_rowid,
    x_blob,

    x_xmltype,
    x_longstring,

    // Deprecated synonyms.
    x_short = x_int16,
    x_integer = x_int32,
    x_long_long = x_int64,
    x_unsigned_long_long = x_uint64
};
objects.description: Internal enumeration describing the C++ exchange types used for binding/fetching between user code and backend implementations, including deprecated aliases.
Optimization hint for statement preparation: single-shot versus repeatable execution.
Abstract backend interface for binding a single value "into" a statement result. Backends implement lifecycle hooks for fetching and cleanup.
Abstract backend interface for binding a vector of results for bulk fetch operations, with size management and lifecycle hooks.
Abstract backend interface for binding a single input/output parameter ("use"). Supports binding by position or name and pre/post use hooks.
Abstract backend interface for binding vectors of input/output parameters for bulk operations.
Abstract backend interface representing a prepared/executed SQL statement. Creates bind/fetch backends, executes/fetches, describes results, and exposes bookkeeping flags.
Abstract backend holder for database-specific ROWID/OID values.
Abstract backend interface for BLOB I/O associated with a session. Provides length, read/write/append, trim, and access to owning session backend.

Abstract backend interface representing a database session/connection. Manages transactions, DDL helpers, metadata queries, auto-generated values, and creates statement/rowid/blob backends. Holds pointers to failover callback and owning soci::session.
Abstract factory for creating session_backend instances for a specific RDBMS backend, given connection_parameters.

objects.definition: typedef void * session_handle;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a SOCI database session/connection. It is a typedef to void*, managed via the provided C API. Lifetime is created by soci_create_session() and must be destroyed with soci_destroy_session(). Unknown internal structure.

objects.definition: typedef void *blob_handle;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a SOCI BLOB value associated with a session. Created by soci_create_blob() and destroyed with soci_destroy_blob(). Provides read/write/append/trim and state/error inspection via dedicated functions. Unknown internal representation.

objects.definition: typedef void * statement_handle;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a prepared/executed SOCI statement. Created by soci_create_statement() and destroyed with soci_destroy_statement(). Used to bind inputs/outputs, prepare SQL, execute, fetch, and inspect state/errors. Unknown internal representation.

Alias type that resolves to the signed long-sized integral type that is not already int64_t on this platform: it becomes long if long long is int64_t, otherwise long long. Used to handle the “other” wide signed integer uniformly.

Alias to the fixed-width signed integer type matching the size of soci_l_or_ll_t: int32_t if soci_l_or_ll_t is 4 bytes, otherwise int64_t. Facilitates consistent specialization using fixed-width types.

Alias type that resolves to the unsigned long-sized integral type that is not already uint64_t on this platform: it becomes unsigned long if unsigned long long is uint64_t, otherwise unsigned long long.
Alias to the fixed-width unsigned integer type matching the size of soci_ul_or_ull_t: uint32_t if soci_ul_or_ull_t is 4 bytes, otherwise uint64_t.
Small wrapper struct around int8_t used when char and int8_t are the same type, enabling distinct template specializations from char. Holds a single int8_t value initialized to 0.
Alias resolving to soci_int8_t_wrapper when int8_t is the same type as char (to allow separate template specializations), otherwise resolves directly to int8_t.

Low-level, non-copyable implementation of a database statement in SOCI. Manages parameter binding, result fetching, back-end interaction, and reference counting. Owned and accessed through the handle class soci::statement.
Public, copyable handle for executing SQL statements. Wraps and reference-counts details::statement_impl and exposes its operations to users.
Specialization enabling soci::statement to be used as an INTO target in SOCI bindings. Wraps a statement reference for result extraction semantics.
Specialization enabling soci::statement to be used as a USE parameter in SOCI bindings. Holds a non-const statement reference and optional indicator/name.
Traits specialization identifying soci::statement as a basic SOCI type family member with x_type = x_statement for binding/exchange machinery.

RAII-style transaction guard for soci::session. Constructing it starts a database transaction on the provided session; commit() commits, rollback() rolls back, and the destructor rolls back automatically if neither commit() nor rollback() was called (inferred from handled_ flag). Non-copyable. Owns no resources itself but operates on the referenced session.

Concrete blob_backend implementation that stores BLOB data in an in-memory std::vector<uint8_t>. It provides read/ write/ append/ trim operations against the buffer and exposes the associated session_backend. Intended for use when the underlying database lacks an efficient native BLOB mechanism. It owns a reference to a session_backend and manages its own resizable byte buffer.
Tagged union of pointers to supported SOCI value types. Used internally by holder to store type-erased pointers according to db_type discriminator.
Maps std::string to db_string.
Maps std::wstring to db_wstring.
Maps int8_t to db_int8.
Maps int16_t to db_int16.
Maps int32_t to db_int32.
Maps int64_t to db_int64.
Maps uint8_t to db_uint8.
Maps uint16_t to db_uint16.
Maps uint32_t to db_uint32.
Maps uint64_t to db_uint64.
Maps soci_l_or_ll_t (typedef from soci-types.h) to the same db_type as soci_l_or_ll_int_t via inheritance. The actual enum value depends on the alias type definition outside this header.
Maps soci_ul_or_ull_t (typedef from soci-types.h) to the same db_type as soci_ul_or_ull_int_t via inheritance. Actual mapping depends on external typedef.
Maps double to db_double.
Maps std::tm to db_date.

objects.definition: struct value_cast_tag{};
objects.description: Tag type used to select value-returning get() in holder, which may perform type conversion via soci_cast.

objects.definition: struct value_reference_tag{};
objects.description: Tag type used to select reference-returning get() in holder, which enforces exact type matching.

Type-erased owner of a single value pointer with runtime db_type tag. Provides get() with conversion (value_cast_tag) and exact reference access (value_reference_tag). Destructor deletes the stored pointer according to dt_. Use make_holder(T*) to construct. Ownership semantics: holder takes ownership and will delete with delete; ensure pointer was allocated with new and is not shared.

objects.definition:
template<>
struct is_contiguous_resizable_container<std::string> : std::true_type {};
objects.description: Specialization marking std::string as a contiguous, resizable byte container.

Wrapper type used with SOCI 'into'/'use' to hint databases/drivers that support specialized XML handling. If unsupported, it should be treated equivalently to a plain std::string via its 'value' member. Construction: default or initialize 'value'. No special destruction beyond std::string. Unknown additional semantics beyond hinting.

Wrapper type for very long textual data with SOCI 'into'/'use'. Intended to guide backends that have special handling for long text (e.g., CLOB). If unsupported, it degrades to std::string through the 'value' field. Construct by setting 'value'. No special destruction beyond std::string. Specific backend limits/behaviors are unspecified here.

Abstract base class for objects handling binding of input data (and OUT PL/SQL variables) to a statement. Provides lifecycle hooks for binding, execution, conversion, and cleanup, and exposes size for single or vector bindings.

objects.definition: typedef type_ptr<use_type_base> use_type_ptr;
objects.description: Smart-pointer typedef wrapping use_type_base. Exact ownership semantics depend on type_ptr from soci/type-ptr.h (likely intrusive or shared pointer). Pointer form here is use_type_ptr *.

Concrete use_type_base for binding a single value of a supported exchange_type. Holds raw data pointer, optional indicator, read-only flag, and backend handle. Provides hooks to convert between user and base types via convert_to_base/from_base.

Concrete use_type_base for binding vectors (bulk bindings). Supports optional indicator vector, subrange [begin, *end), and backend handle. Designed for base-type vectors with optional conversion hook.

objects.definition: typedef void no_indicator;
objects.description: Marker type indicating that no indicator is used for a given binding. Serves solely as a tag in use_container specializations and overload resolution.

Template specialization declaring exchange traits for soci::values. It associates the values type with the basic_type_tag family and provides a dummy enumerator required by the SOCI template machinery. Used by SOCI to drive type-dependent binding/exchange behavior.

Template specialization of use_type for soci::values. Acts as a binder of a values object to a statement for use (input) parameters. Manages name formatting, binding, lifecycle hooks (pre_use, post_use, clean_up), and offers virtual hooks for conversion to/from base types. Requires a reference to an existing values instance; it does not own it.
direct_api_constructors: soci::details::use_type<soci::values>::use_type(values & v, indicator ind, std::string const & name)

objects.description: Disabled/forbidden specialization of use_type for std::vector<values>. It declares a private default constructor and no public interface to prevent bulk ORM usage with values. This is an incomplete/unspecified non-constructible placeholder.

Template specialization of into_type for soci::values, used to receive result rows (output) into a values object. It forwards to into_type<row> using the row contained in values and ensures the values instance is cleaned up after use. It does not own the referenced values.

Disabled/forbidden specialization of into_type for std::vector<values>. It declares a private default constructor and no public interface to prevent bulk ORM usage with values. This is an incomplete/unspecified non-constructible placeholder.
Abstract polymorphic base used to own deep-copied values of arbitrary types for later use/binding. Provides a virtual destructor for safe deletion via base pointer.

A dynamic container-like facade for holding and accessing heterogeneous values corresponding to SQL result columns or bound parameters. It can read values by index or name, manage NULL via indicators, and stage values for use/bind by converting user types to their base database types and storing deep copies. Lifetimes of internal buffers are managed manually; clean_up() releases internal allocations.

Backend adapter for mapping a single result value (standard into) when using the "empty" SOCI backend. It implements the standard_into_type_backend interface and delegates to its owning empty_statement_backend via reference.
Backend adapter for mapping a vector of result values (vector into) in the empty backend. Holds a reference to the parent empty_statement_backend.
Backend adapter for binding a single input/output value (standard use) for statements in the empty backend.
Backend adapter for binding vectors of values (vector use) in the empty backend. Maintains a reference to the owning empty_statement_backend.
Implements the SOCI statement backend for the "empty" backend, providing lifecycle, execution, fetch, and factory methods for into/use backends. Holds a reference to its owning empty_session_backend.
Implements the rowid handle for the empty backend. Constructed with an empty_session_backend.
Implements BLOB operations for the empty backend. Holds a reference to the constructing empty_session_backend and exposes it via get_session_backend.
Implements the SOCI session backend for the empty backend. Always reports connected, provides transaction stubs, and factories for statements, rowids, and blobs.
Factory for creating empty_session_backend instances; used by SOCI to register and obtain the "empty" backend.

objects.definition: struct empty_statement_backend;
objects.description: Forward declaration of empty_statement_backend. Full definition provided later in this header.

objects.definition: struct empty_session_backend;
objects.description: Forward declaration of empty_session_backend. Full definition provided later in this header.

functions.name: soci::dynamic_backends::get
functions.description: Returns a reference to the backend_factory corresponding to the given backend name. Intended for internal use by the SOCI library; external callers generally should not use this directly. Typical usage is to obtain an implementation for a named backend so it can be used to create sessions or statements. Details of how backends are located/loaded are not visible here.
requirements: Intended for internal use only; external code should prefer higher-level APIs.
Every successful call to get(name) must be matched by a corresponding unget(name) call with the same name to release internal resources.
The provided name should identify a backend known to the dynamic backend loader; behavior if unknown is not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: soci::dynamic_backends::unget
functions.description: Releases a backend_factory previously obtained with get(name). Intended for internal use; pairs with get() to balance resource/reference tracking performed by the loader.
requirements: Must be called to match a prior successful get(name) call, using the exact same name.
Should not be called unless a corresponding get(name) was previously successful; behavior otherwise is unspecified here (unknown).

functions.name: soci::dynamic_backends::search_paths
functions.description: Returns a modifiable reference to the collection of filesystem search paths used by the dynamic backend loader to locate backend shared libraries. Provided for advanced user-level management to inspect or adjust where the loader looks for backends.
requirements: The returned reference refers to internal state of the loader; modifying it will affect subsequent backend discovery (exact lifetime and thread-safety characteristics are not documented here; unknown).
Callers should only store or modify valid filesystem path strings; behavior for invalid paths is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: soci::dynamic_backends::register_backend
functions.signature: SOCI_DECL void register_backend(std::string const & name, std::string const & shared_object = std::string());
functions.description: Registers a backend under the given name, optionally associating it with a specific shared object (dynamic library) path to be used by the loader. Intended for advanced user-level management to make additional backends available by name.
requirements: name identifies the backend to register; constraints on format or emptiness are not specified here (unknown).
If shared_object is provided, it should denote a loadable shared library containing the backend implementation; exact requirements (existence, ABI compatibility) are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: soci::dynamic_backends::register_backend
functions.signature: SOCI_DECL void register_backend(std::string const & name, backend_factory const & factory);
functions.description: Registers a backend under the given name using an explicit backend_factory instance rather than a shared library. Allows embedding or programmatic provision of a backend implementation.
requirements: name identifies the backend to register; constraints on format or uniqueness are not specified here (unknown).
The factory object is passed by const reference; whether it is copied or must outlive registration is not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: soci::dynamic_backends::list_all
functions.description: Returns the list of names of all currently known/registered dynamic backends. Useful for discovery or diagnostics.

functions.name: soci::dynamic_backends::unload
functions.description: Unloads the backend identified by name, releasing any resources associated with it in the dynamic backend loader. Provided for advanced user-level control.
requirements: name must refer to a backend currently managed by the loader; behavior if not registered or already unloaded is not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: soci::dynamic_backends::unload_all
functions.description: Unloads all dynamically managed backends, releasing associated resources. Provided for advanced user-level control or cleanup.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_vector::exchange
functions.description: Transfers ownership of a prepared use_type object into this use_type_vector and stores it. Intended to enqueue a single bound input value for a statement. After pushing the raw pointer, the smart wrapper releases ownership so the vector manages lifetime and will delete the object in its destructor.
requirements: u must reference a dynamically allocated use_type_base-compatible object managed by use_type_ptr; ownership is transferred to the vector and the object will be deleted by the vector destructor
After the call, the use_type_ptr no longer owns the object (release() is called); the caller must not delete the object or assume ownership remains
This function does not perform null checks; passing a null pointer would result in storing a null entry (delete-null is safe but likely unintended)
Thread-safety is not specified; concurrent access to the same use_type_vector must be externally synchronized

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_vector::exchange_
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Indicator>
void soci::details::use_type_vector::exchange_(use_container<T, Indicator> const &uc, boost::mpl::true_ * /* fusion sequence */)
functions.description: Internal dispatch used when T is detected as a Boost Fusion sequence: iterates over uc.t and enqueues a use() binding for each element, carrying uc.ind. Used by exchange().
requirements: Available only when SOCI_HAVE_BOOST is defined and T satisfies boost::fusion::traits::is_sequence<T>
uc.t must be a valid Boost Fusion sequence; each element must be bindable with use(element, uc.ind)
uc.ind must be a valid Indicator object compatible with the bound elements
Private helper; not intended to be called directly by user code

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_vector::exchange
functions.description: Transfers ownership of a prepared into_type object into this into_type_vector and stores it. Intended to enqueue a single output binding (destination for fetched data). After pushing the raw pointer, the smart wrapper releases ownership so the vector manages lifetime and will delete the object in its destructor.
requirements: i must reference a dynamically allocated into_type_base-compatible object managed by into_type_ptr; ownership is transferred to the vector and the object will be deleted by the vector destructor
After the call, the into_type_ptr no longer owns the object (release() is called); the caller must not delete the object or assume ownership remains
This function does not perform null checks; passing a null pointer would result in storing a null entry (delete-null is safe but likely unintended)
Thread-safety is not specified; concurrent access to the same into_type_vector must be externally synchronized

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_vector::exchange_
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Indicator>
void soci::details::into_type_vector::exchange_(into_container<T, Indicator> const &ic, boost::mpl::true_ * /* fusion sequence */)
functions.description: Internal dispatch used when T is detected as a Boost Fusion sequence: iterates over ic.t and enqueues an into() binding for each element, carrying ic.ind. Used by exchange().
requirements: Available only when SOCI_HAVE_BOOST is defined and T satisfies boost::fusion::traits::is_sequence<T>
ic.t must be a valid Boost Fusion sequence; each element must be bindable with into(element, ic.ind)
ic.ind must be a valid Indicator object compatible with the bound elements
Private helper; not intended to be called directly by user code

functions.name: soci::blob::blob
functions.description: Default-constructs a blob in an invalid/uninitialized state. Typically followed by a call to initialize(session) or initialize(details::blob_backend*), or move-assignment from another valid blob, before use.
requirements: Object is invalid after default construction until explicitly initialized via initialize(session) or initialize(details::blob_backend*), or assigned from a valid blob.
Do not call data-manipulation functions (get_len, read/read_from_start, write/write_from_start, append, trim, get_backend use) until the blob is valid (see is_valid).

functions.name: soci::blob::~blob
functions.description: Destroys the blob and releases any associated backend resources.
requirements: The blob must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: soci::blob::operator=
functions.description: Move-assigns from other, releasing current resources (if any) and taking ownership of other's backend handle.
requirements: Self-assignment with the same object is permitted but has no effect beyond standard move semantics.
After move-assignment, other is in a moved-from state and should only be destroyed, re-initialized, or re-assigned before further use.

functions.name: soci::blob::is_valid
functions.description: Returns true if the blob is currently in a valid/initialized state and can be used for I/O operations; false otherwise.

functions.name: soci::blob::initialize
functions.description: (Re)initializes the blob using the provided SOCI session, making it valid for I/O operations.
requirements: s must refer to a valid, active soci::session compatible with this blob instance.
Safe to call on an invalid blob to initialize it; behavior on reinitializing an already valid blob is backend-specific/unknown.

functions.name: soci::blob::initialize
functions.description: Initializes the blob by taking ownership of an existing backend-specific blob handle.
requirements: backend must be a valid pointer to a backend-specific blob implementation compatible with this SOCI build.
Ownership/lifetime after passing the pointer is managed by soci::blob; passing an already-managed or invalid pointer results in undefined/unknown behavior.
Passing nullptr will leave the blob invalid.

functions.name: soci::blob::get_len
functions.description: Returns the current size, in bytes, of the blob.
requirements: The blob should be in a valid state (is_valid() == true) before calling; behavior if invalid is backend-specific/unknown.

functions.name: soci::blob::read
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::blob::read(std::size_t offset, void * buf, std::size_t toRead);
functions.description: Deprecated. Reads up to toRead bytes from the blob into buf using a backend-specific offset scheme. Returns the number of bytes actually read. Prefer read_from_start for well-defined semantics.
requirements: The blob must be valid before calling.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least toRead bytes when toRead > 0; if toRead == 0, buf may be nullptr.
offset semantics are backend-specific; callers must ensure offset is valid for the target backend to avoid exceptions or errors.

functions.name: soci::blob::read_from_start
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::blob::read_from_start(void * buf, std::size_t toRead, std::size_t offset = 0);
functions.description: Reads up to toRead bytes starting at byte offset from the beginning of the blob (offset 0 is the start). Copies into buf and returns the number of bytes actually read. Using an offset > 0 that is >= the blob size throws an exception.
requirements: The blob must be valid before calling.
buf must point to a writable memory region of at least toRead bytes when toRead > 0; if toRead == 0, buf may be nullptr.
offset must be 0, or if > 0 it must be strictly less than the current blob size; otherwise an exception is thrown.
toRead may be larger than the available data; the function returns the number of bytes actually read.

functions.name: soci::blob::write
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::blob::write(std::size_t offset, const void * buf, std::size_t toWrite);
functions.description: Deprecated. Writes up to toWrite bytes from buf into the blob using a backend-specific offset scheme. Returns the number of bytes actually written. Prefer write_from_start for well-defined semantics.
requirements: The blob must be valid before calling.
buf must point to a readable memory region of at least toWrite bytes when toWrite > 0; if toWrite == 0, buf may be nullptr.
offset semantics are backend-specific; callers must ensure offset is valid for the target backend to avoid exceptions or errors.

functions.name: soci::blob::write_from_start
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::blob::write_from_start(const void * buf, std::size_t toWrite, std::size_t offset = 0);
functions.description: Writes up to toWrite bytes from buf into the blob starting at byte offset from the beginning (offset starts at 0). Returns the number of bytes actually written.
requirements: The blob must be valid before calling.
buf must point to a readable memory region of at least toWrite bytes when toWrite > 0; if toWrite == 0, buf may be nullptr.
offset must be a non-negative byte index from the start (0-based). Specific limits on maximum offset or extension/truncation behavior are backend-specific/unknown.

functions.name: soci::blob::append
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::blob::append(const void * buf, std::size_t toWrite);
functions.description: Appends up to toWrite bytes from buf to the end of the blob. Returns the number of bytes actually written.
requirements: The blob must be valid before calling.
buf must point to a readable memory region of at least toWrite bytes when toWrite > 0; if toWrite == 0, buf may be nullptr.

functions.name: soci::blob::trim
functions.description: Truncates or resizes the blob to newLen bytes. Intended primarily for truncation (reducing size). Behavior when newLen exceeds the current size is not documented here and may be backend-specific.
requirements: The blob must be valid before calling.

newLen must be a non-negative size in bytes. Whether newLen may exceed the current size is unknown; callers should assume truncation semantics and avoid passing values larger than the current size unless confirmed for the backend.

functions.name: soci::blob::get_backend
functions.description: Returns the underlying backend blob handle pointer managed by this object, or nullptr if the blob is not initialized. Exposes backend-specific functionality when needed.
requirements: The returned pointer may be nullptr if the blob is invalid; callers must check before use.
The lifetime of the returned pointer is managed by soci::blob; do not delete it or store it beyond the lifetime of the blob.
Backend-specific operations performed via this pointer must follow the backend's own API contracts.

functions.name: soci::failover_callback::failover_callback
functions.description: Default constructor for the failover_callback interface. Intended to be used as a base class for user-defined callbacks that receive failover notifications from SOCI.
requirements: No arguments or preconditions.
Typically used by constructing a derived class instance and passing it to SOCI components that support failover callbacks.

functions.name: soci::failover_callback::~failover_callback
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the failover_callback interface, enabling safe destruction via a base-class pointer.
requirements: No arguments or preconditions.
Derived classes should ensure any overridden destructor remains noexcept-safe if used in callback contexts (not stated by the header; general C++ best practice).

functions.name: soci::failover_callback::started
functions.description: Called when a failover operation has started after discovering connectivity problems. Default implementation does nothing; override in a derived class to observe or log start of failover.
requirements: No arguments or preconditions.
May be overridden by user code; if overridden, it should be prepared to be called when a connection issue is detected.

functions.name: soci::failover_callback::finished
functions.description: Called after successful failover when a new connection has been created. The provided session reference denotes the new connection and can be used to replay initialization commands (e.g., session configuration). Default implementation does nothing; override to perform post-reconnect setup.
requirements: Parameter sql must refer to a valid soci::session representing the newly established connection (as implied by the comment).
Caller (SOCI) supplies sql; user override may issue commands using this session.

functions.name: soci::failover_callback::failed
functions.signature: virtual void soci::failover_callback::failed(bool & retry, std::string & newTarget)
functions.description: Called when an attempt to reconnect failed. User code can set retry to true to request another reconnection attempt. newTarget can be assigned a connection string hint for subsequent attempts; it may be ignored by backends or external mechanisms. Default implementation does nothing.
requirements: On return, set retry to true to request another reconnection attempt; leave false to stop retrying (as implied by the comment).
If provided, assign newTarget to a connection string hint appropriate for the backend; it may be ignored.
Both parameters are out-parameters from the user override’s perspective and must remain valid lvalues during the call (enforced by references).

functions.name: soci::failover_callback::aborted
functions.description: Called when there was a failure that prevents further failover attempts. Default implementation does nothing; override to log or notify that failover will not continue.
requirements: No arguments or preconditions.
May be overridden to perform cleanup or notifications when failover is terminal.

functions.name: soci::type_conversion<soci::column_info>::get_numeric_value
functions.signature: static std::size_t soci::type_conversion<soci::column_info>::get_numeric_value(const soci::values & v, const std::string & field_name)
functions.description: Helper used during column_info conversion to extract a size_t from a soci::values record. It inspects the db_type of the specified field and reads it using the corresponding typed getter, converting the result to std::size_t. For unsupported/non-numeric types it returns 0. Typical usage is internal to from_base() to read length, precision, and scale fields from database metadata rows.
requirements: v must contain a field named exactly field_name; v.get_properties(field_name) must be valid for that field.
The field's db_type should be one of: db_double, db_int8, db_uint8, db_int16, db_uint16, db_int32, db_uint32, db_int64, db_uint64 to yield a non-zero meaningful value; otherwise 0 is returned.
If the field exists but its value is NULL, SOCI's v.get<T>(field_name, default) will use the provided default (0/0.0) before conversion.
Callers should expect SOCI to throw if field_name is missing or if properties cannot be retrieved.

functions.name: soci::type_conversion<soci::column_info>::from_base
functions.signature: static void soci::type_conversion<soci::column_info>::from_base(const soci::values & v, soci::indicator ind, soci::column_info & ci)
functions.description: Populates a soci::column_info structure from a soci::values row representing column metadata. It reads well-known metadata fields (COLUMN_NAME, CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH, NUMERIC_PRECISION, NUMERIC_SCALE, DATA_TYPE, IS_NULLABLE), infers both legacy data_type and db_type from DATA_TYPE (with special handling for numeric scale), and sets nullable based on IS_NULLABLE == "YES". Intended to be used by SOCI's type conversion framework when mapping result-set metadata to column_info.
requirements: v must provide the following fields with the exact names used by the implementation: "COLUMN_NAME" (string), "CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH" (numeric), "NUMERIC_PRECISION" (numeric), "NUMERIC_SCALE" (numeric), "DATA_TYPE" (string), and "IS_NULLABLE" (string).
Numeric fields should have db_type among the supported numeric types so get_numeric_value() can read them; otherwise they will be treated as 0.
The indicator parameter is ignored by this implementation; callers may pass any value.
ci must be a valid reference to an existing soci::column_info to be filled in.
Type inference is based on substring/case checks of DATA_TYPE; unrecognized types default to string/db_string. Callers should not rely on more precise mapping without adapting this function.
If any required field is missing or of an incompatible type, SOCI may throw during v.get_properties(...) or v.get<...>(...).

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::connection_parameters
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty set of connection parameters. Intended as a starting point to later set the backend and connection string/options programmatically.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::~connection_parameters
functions.description: Destructor for connection parameters. Releases any internal references (e.g., to a dynamic backend).

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::get_factory
functions.description: Returns the backend_factory pointer associated with these parameters, if any.
requirements: Return value may be null if constructed without an explicit backend or if the backend is resolved lazily; callers must check for null before use.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::set_connect_string
functions.description: Sets or replaces the stored connection string to be used when opening a session.
requirements: connectString should follow the syntax expected by the target backend (not enforced here).

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::get_connect_string
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the currently stored connection string.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid as long as the connection_parameters object remains alive and the string is not modified by subsequent setters on the same object.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::extract_options_from_space_separated_string
functions.description: Parses the current connection string as space-separated name=value pairs and stores them as options. Unknown option names are ignored. Throws on invalid syntax (e.g., a name without a corresponding value).
requirements: The current connect string should use space-separated name=value syntax for options.
Callers must be prepared to handle exceptions on invalid syntax.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::build_string_from_options
functions.description: Builds and returns a space-separated connection string from the stored options, quoting option values using the provided quote character.
requirements: quote is an arbitrary character used to quote values; behavior for special characters is not specified in this header.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::set_option
functions.signature: void soci::connection_parameters::set_option(const char * name, std::string const & value)
functions.description: Sets or overwrites the value of an option by name.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
Overwrites any existing value for the given option name.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::get_option
functions.signature: bool soci::connection_parameters::get_option(const char * name, std::string & value) const
functions.description: Looks up an option by name and, if found, assigns its value to the output parameter and returns true; returns false if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
value must be a valid reference; its previous contents will be overwritten if the option is found.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::has_option
functions.description: Checks whether an option with the given name exists.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::extract_option
functions.description: Retrieves an option value by name and removes the option from the internal set if found. Returns true on success, false if the option does not exist.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
value must be a valid reference; its previous contents will be overwritten if the option is found.
Callers should not expect the option to remain present after a successful call.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::is_true_value
functions.signature: static bool soci::connection_parameters::is_true_value(const char * name, std::string const & value)
functions.description: Interprets an option value as a boolean in a case-insensitive manner. Returns true for "1", "yes", "true", "on", or empty string; returns false for "0", "no", "false", or "off". Throws an exception if the value is specified but not one of the recognized forms.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer (used only for diagnostics).
value should be one of the recognized true/false tokens; callers must be prepared to handle exceptions for unrecognized values.

functions.name: soci::connection_parameters::is_option_on
functions.description: Convenience check for whether an option is present and evaluates to true per is_true_value(). Returns false if the option is not present. Propagates any exception from is_true_value() for invalid values.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string pointer.
Callers must be prepared to handle exceptions if the option is present but has an unrecognized boolean value.

functions.name: soci::connection_pool::connection_pool
functions.description: Constructs a pool of database sessions with the given number of slots. Typical usage is to create a pool early in application setup, obtain references to individual session objects via at(i) to configure/open them, and later lease/give_back slots for concurrent use.
requirements: size is the number of slots in the pool; valid range details are unknown from this header
The pool object must remain alive while any of its sessions or leased slots are in use
Thread-safety guarantees, memory ownership, and exception behavior are unknown from this header

functions.name: soci::connection_pool::~connection_pool
functions.description: Destroys the connection pool and releases its resources. Intended to be called when the pool is no longer needed.
requirements: Do not access the pool or any of its facilities after destruction
Whether outstanding leases are allowed at destruction time is unknown from this header

functions.name: soci::connection_pool::at
functions.description: Returns a reference to the session object stored at slot index pos. Typically used to initialize or configure the session in a given pool slot (e.g., open a connection) before leasing.
requirements: pos must refer to a valid slot index in the pool; the valid range is [0, size) where size was provided at construction
Returned reference must not be used after the pool is destroyed
Thread-safety and whether concurrent calls to at are allowed are unknown from this header

functions.name: soci::connection_pool::lease
functions.description: Obtains (leases) a free slot from the pool and returns its index. Intended to be paired with give_back(pos) when the caller is done using the leased session.
requirements: The returned index must later be returned to the same pool by calling give_back(pos) exactly once
Behavior when no slots are immediately available (e.g., blocking vs. throwing) is unknown from this header
The pool must outlive the use of the leased slot

functions.name: soci::connection_pool::try_lease
functions.description: Attempts to lease a free slot from the pool, storing the slot index in pos on success. Returns true if a slot was obtained within the specified timeout, false otherwise. Useful for bounded-wait acquisition.
requirements: On success (returning true), the caller must later return the leased slot by calling give_back(pos) exactly once
The time unit, valid range, and semantics of timeout are not specified in this header and are therefore unknown
Whether pos is modified on failure is unknown; callers should not rely on its value when the function returns false
The pool must outlive the use of any leased slot

functions.name: soci::connection_pool::give_back
functions.description: Returns a previously leased slot identified by pos back to the pool, making it available for others to lease.
requirements: pos must be a valid pool index previously obtained from lease() or try_lease() on the same pool and not yet returned
pos must be within the pool’s slot range [0, size)
Do not call give_back more than once for the same lease
Behavior when passing an invalid or already returned index is unknown from this header

functions.name: soci::soci_error::soci_error
functions.description: Constructs a SOCI exception with the specified error message. Intended to be thrown by SOCI when an error occurs; stores the message (without context). Use get_error_message() to retrieve the original message and what() for the full message with context (if any).
requirements: msg can be any valid std::string; no format or content is required.
The constructed object follows std::exception semantics and may be thrown and caught by reference.

functions.name: soci::soci_error::operator=
functions.description: Assigns this soci_error from another one, replacing the current error state with that of e.
requirements: The source object e must be a valid soci::soci_error instance.
No exceptions are thrown during assignment (noexcept).

functions.name: soci::soci_error::~soci_error
functions.description: Destroys the soci_error object. Overrides std::runtime_error destructor; no resources are expected to escape and destruction is noexcept.
requirements: No specific caller requirements; safe to destroy when no longer needed.
Do not use pointers returned by what() after the object is destroyed.

functions.name: soci::soci_error::get_error_message
functions.description: Returns just the base error message provided at construction time, without any added context. Useful when the raw message (without stack of contexts) is required.
requirements: Can be called on any valid soci_error instance.
Does not throw as per typical accessor expectations, but exception-safety is not explicitly documented (unknown).

functions.name: soci::soci_error::what
functions.description: Returns the full error message as a C string, combining the original message with any accumulated context records. Overrides std::exception::what().
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid as long as the soci_error object is alive and unchanged, consistent with std::exception::what() semantics.
Callers must not modify or free the returned pointer.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept).

functions.name: soci::soci_error::add_context
functions.description: Appends additional contextual information to the exception, intended to be called by SOCI internals as the exception propagates. The first added context should correspond to the lowest level and the last to the highest level.
requirements: Intended for use by SOCI itself; external callers should normally not call this function.
May be called multiple times; the order of calls should reflect low-to-high context as the exception bubbles up.
context can be any valid std::string.

functions.name: soci::soci_error::get_error_category
functions.description: Returns a basic classification of the error. The base implementation returns unknown; backends or derived classes may override to provide a specific category.
requirements: Can be called on any valid soci_error instance.
Return value is one of the error_category enum values; base class returns error_category::unknown.

functions.name: soci::soci_error::get_backend_name
functions.description: Returns the name of the database backend that originated the error, or an empty string if the error is from core SOCI. The base implementation returns an empty string; backends/derived classes may override.
requirements: Can be called on any valid soci_error instance.
Empty string indicates no backend-specific origin in the base class.

functions.name: soci::soci_error::get_backend_error_code
functions.description: Returns a backend-specific integer error code, or 0 if not applicable. The base implementation returns 0; backends/derived classes may override to expose native error codes.
requirements: Can be called on any valid soci_error instance.
0 indicates no backend-specific error code in the base class.

functions.name: soci::soci_error::get_sqlstate
functions.description: Returns the 5-character SQLSTATE associated with the error, or an empty string if not applicable. The base implementation returns an empty string; backends/derived classes may override.
requirements: Can be called on any valid soci_error instance.
Empty string indicates no SQLSTATE in the base class.
If provided by a backend, SQLSTATE is expected to be a 5-character code (exact format enforcement unknown).

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_base::~into_type_base
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the abstract base class that represents an output binding ("into" binding) in SOCI. Ensures proper cleanup via dynamic dispatch when deleting through a base pointer. Typically invoked by SOCI internals when a binding object’s lifetime ends.
requirements: Must be invoked on a fully constructed soci::details::into_type_base-derived object.
Object must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_base::define
functions.description: Pure virtual hook used by SOCI to bind/define the output storage to a backend statement at a given positional index. Implemented by concrete into types to register the output column(s) before execution.
requirements: st must reference a valid, initialized soci::details::statement_impl ready for binding.
position must refer to the current 1-based (?) positional column index; implementers increment/update it to reflect bound columns. Exact indexing convention is backend-defined and not specified here.
Called before statement execution; intended for SOCI internals rather than user code.

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_base::pre_exec
functions.description: Pure virtual callback invoked before executing a statement, allowing the binding to prepare for fetching up to num rows (e.g., allocate buffers).
requirements: num is the number of rows expected/requested for the next execution or fetch cycle; must be non-negative.
Called by SOCI internals prior to execution/fetch; not intended for direct user calls.

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_base::pre_fetch
functions.description: Pure virtual callback invoked immediately before fetching data to let the binding prepare internal state or buffers.
requirements: Called by SOCI internals; underlying statement must have been defined/bound already via define().
No arguments; implementers must ensure internal storage is ready to receive data.

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_base::post_fetch
functions.description: Pure virtual callback invoked after a fetch operation to transfer data from backend buffers into user storage and update indicators. gotData indicates whether any data was retrieved. calledFromFetch distinguishes the call context.
requirements: gotData is true if at least one row of data was obtained; implementers must handle both true and false.
calledFromFetch indicates whether this was triggered by fetch() versus execute(); implementers may adjust behavior accordingly.
Called by SOCI internals; user storage referenced by the binding must still be valid.

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_base::clean_up
functions.description: Pure virtual method to release backend-specific resources associated with the binding (buffers, handles). Called when the binding is no longer needed.
requirements: Called by SOCI internals when the statement/binding is being destroyed or re-bound.
Implementations must be idempotent or safe to call exactly once per binding lifecycle.

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_base::size
functions.description: Returns the number of logical elements represented by this into binding (1 for scalar bindings; N for vector bindings). Used by SOCI to manage bulk operations.
requirements: Must be callable after define() and before/after fetch to report the current capacity/extent.
Implementations must not throw under normal circumstances.

functions.name: soci::details::into_type_base::resize
functions.description: Optional hook for vector bindings to adjust their capacity/length to hold sz elements. Default base implementation is a no-op; vector bindings override it.
requirements: sz is the desired new number of elements for vector bindings; must be a reasonable size for the underlying container.
Only meaningful for vector-based implementations; scalar bindings typically ignore it.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_into_type::standard_into_type
functions.description: Constructs a scalar (standard) into binding for a single value of the given SOCI exchange_type, storing results at data. No indicator is provided; null-state handling depends on backend defaults.
requirements: data must point to valid, writable storage of the exact C++ base type corresponding to type.
The pointed-to storage must outlive the binding, statement execution, and all fetch operations.
type must be a valid soci::exchange_type matching the actual storage type at data.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_into_type::~standard_into_type
functions.description: Destructor for the scalar into binding. Releases backend resources and disconnects the binding from the statement.
requirements: Must be called when no further use of the binding will occur and the underlying storage is still valid.
Not intended to be invoked directly; called automatically when the object goes out of scope or via base pointer deletion.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type::vector_into_type
functions.description: Constructs a vector into binding for bulk fetches into a std::vector of elements described by type. No indicator vector and no range control are provided.
requirements: data must point to a valid std::vector<T> instance whose T corresponds to type; it must be writable and outlive the binding and fetches.
type must match the vector element base type.
Vector capacity/size management may be handled via resize(); vector must tolerate being resized by the binding.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type::~vector_into_type
functions.description: Destructor for the vector into binding. Releases backend state and disconnects the bulk binding.
requirements: Should be called only when the binding is no longer needed and no further fetches will occur.
Automatically invoked when the object is destroyed; not intended for direct calls.

functions.name: soci::details::into_type::into_type
functions.description: Template helper that constructs a standard_into_type for a basic type T supported by SOCI (via exchange_traits<T>::x_type). Binds t as the destination for a single value without an indicator.
requirements: T must have exchange_traits<T>::x_type defined and correspond to a supported SOCI basic type.
t must be a valid lvalue that remains alive and writable for the duration of statement execution and fetches.

functions.name: soci::details::do_into
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::into_type_ptr soci::details::do_into(T & t, soci::details::basic_type_tag)
functions.description: Factory helper that wraps a scalar lvalue t of a basic type T into a heap-allocated into binding (standard_into_type) and returns it as into_type_ptr. Used by SOCI’s into() API for basic types without indicators.
requirements: T must be a SOCI-supported basic type (exchange_traits<T>::x_type defined).
t must be a valid lvalue that remains alive and writable for the duration of the statement execution/fetches.
basic_type_tag is a dispatch token provided by SOCI; callers should pass the correct tag.

functions.name: soci::into
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::into_container<T, soci::details::no_indicator> soci::into(T & t);
functions.description: Creates a bind helper object for extracting a single value of type T from a SOCI statement without an indicator. Intended usage: pass the result to statement preparation/execution APIs (e.g., once << into(var)) to receive a single column value into t.
requirements: t must be an lvalue reference to a variable of a type supported by SOCI extraction.
t must remain valid for the duration of the statement execution that uses the returned helper object.
This function only prepares an extraction helper; it does not perform any I/O by itself.

functions.name: soci::into
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Indicator>
soci::details::into_container<T, Indicator> soci::into(T & t, Indicator & ind);
functions.description: Creates a bind helper object for extracting a single value of type T along with a separate indicator object (e.g., to track NULL) during SOCI statement execution. Intended usage: pass the result to SOCI statement APIs.
requirements: t must be an lvalue reference to a variable of a type supported by SOCI extraction.
ind must be an lvalue reference to an indicator-like object compatible with SOCI (commonly soci::indicator).
Both t and ind must remain valid for the duration of the statement execution that uses the returned helper object.
This function only prepares an extraction helper; it does not perform any I/O by itself.

functions.name: soci::into
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::into_type_ptr soci::into(T & t, std::size_t bufSize);
functions.description: Creates a heap-allocated SOCI extraction helper for types requiring a runtime buffer size (comment indicates use for character buffers). Intended usage: pass the returned pointer-like helper to SOCI statement APIs to extract into t with the given buffer size.
requirements: t must be an lvalue reference and of a type for which details::into_type<T>(t, bufSize) is valid (typically a character buffer such as char* or char array).
bufSize must specify the usable capacity of t in bytes/characters; it should be greater than 0 and large enough to hold the incoming data including any required terminator for character buffers.
t must remain valid for the duration of the statement execution that uses the returned helper.
Memory management of the returned details::into_type_ptr is handled by SOCI; callers should not delete it directly.

functions.name: soci::into
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::into_type_ptr soci::into(std::vector<T> & t, std::size_t begin, std::size_t & end);
functions.description: Creates a SOCI extraction helper for bulk fetching into a subrange of a vector t. The begin index specifies the starting position in t; end is provided by reference and will be updated by SOCI to indicate the end position or number of elements processed.
requirements: t must be an lvalue reference to a std::vector of a type supported by SOCI bulk extraction.
begin specifies the starting index within the logical range to fill; it should be within the valid range for bulk operations (typically begin <= t.size()).
end must be an lvalue reference to a std::size_t that SOCI can modify to report how many elements were produced or the end index.
t (and end) must remain valid for the duration of the statement execution that uses the returned helper.
The precise interpretation of begin/end (count vs. index) depends on SOCI implementation; callers should consult SOCI docs if uncertain.

functions.name: soci::into
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::into_type_ptr soci::into(std::vector<T> & t, std::vector<indicator> & ind);
functions.description: Creates a SOCI extraction helper for bulk fetching into a vector t with a parallel vector of indicators ind to report per-element null/indicator status.
requirements: t must be an lvalue reference to a std::vector whose element type T is supported by SOCI bulk extraction.
ind must be an lvalue reference to a std::vector<soci::indicator>-compatible type (here, indicator is in scope).
Both t and ind must remain valid for the duration of the statement execution that uses the returned helper.
The expected size relationship between t and ind is determined by SOCI; typically they should correspond element-for-element. If uncertain, consult SOCI documentation.

functions.name: soci::query_parameter::query_parameter
functions.description: Constructs a query_parameter with an optional name and value. Intended to represent a single bound parameter (name/value) for logging. Defaults to empty strings for both fields when not provided.
requirements: name may be empty; no constraints specified.
value may be empty; no constraints specified.
Object may be constructed with default arguments or explicit strings; both arguments are copied/moved into the instance.

functions.name: soci::logger_impl::~logger_impl
functions.description: Virtual destructor for logger_impl, allowing proper cleanup via base-class pointers. Override in derived classes if custom cleanup is needed.
requirements: Must be invoked through a valid soci::logger_impl object (typically via delete on a pointer owned by a wrapper such as soci::logger).
Derived classes should ensure any resources allocated by them are released in their destructors.

functions.name: soci::logger_impl::start_query
functions.description: Indicates that a new database query is about to be executed. Implementations typically record the query and reset any per-query state. This is the primary hook for logging SQL statements.
requirements: query should contain the SQL text to be executed; may be empty if unknown.
Callers should call this before add_query_parameter() to associate parameters with the active query (implied by documentation).

functions.name: soci::logger_impl::add_query_parameter
functions.description: Logs a parameter bound to the currently active query. Implementations may store or emit the parameter for contextual logging.
requirements: There must be a currently active query initiated by start_query() for the parameter to be meaningful (implied by documentation).
name may be empty; no explicit format enforced.
value may be empty; no explicit format enforced.

functions.name: soci::logger_impl::clear_query_parameters
functions.description: Clears all currently logged query parameters associated with the active query. Typically called when a query completes or before starting a new one.
requirements: Should be called when parameters are no longer relevant or prior to logging a new set of parameters. No other explicit constraints.

functions.name: soci::logger_impl::clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a heap-allocated copy of this logger_impl by calling the derived class’s do_clone(). Used to duplicate logger implementations safely.
requirements: Returns a raw pointer to a heap-allocated soci::logger_impl; the caller assumes ownership and is responsible for deleting the returned pointer.
The underlying derived class must implement do_clone() to return a new heap-allocated copy; otherwise the program will not link/behave correctly.

functions.name: soci::logger_impl::set_stream
functions.description: Compatibility hook to set an output stream used by basic session logging support. Custom logger implementations may override this only if they intend to support session::set_stream-style logging.
requirements: s may be nullptr if disabling stream-based logging (implied by typical set_stream semantics; not explicitly stated).

If overridden, implementations should store the pointer without taking ownership; lifetime management of the stream remains with the caller (implied by conventional stream usage; exact ownership not stated).

functions.name: soci::logger_impl::get_stream
