functions.description: Returns the currently configured output stream for basic session logging, or nullptr if none. Provided for compatibility with session basic logging support.
requirements: May return nullptr if no stream is set.
Caller must not delete the returned stream; ownership is not transferred.

functions.name: soci::logger_impl::get_last_query
functions.description: Returns the last query recorded by the logger, if supported. Used to implement basic session logging compatibility.
requirements: May return an empty string if no query has been recorded.
Availability and exact content depend on the specific logger_impl; not all implementations must track the last query.

functions.name: soci::logger_impl::get_last_query_context
functions.description: Returns a textual context for the last query (e.g., parameters or additional info), if supported. Used for session basic logging compatibility.
requirements: May return an empty string if no context is recorded.
Content and format are implementation-defined and may depend on prior calls to add_query_parameter().

functions.name: soci::logger::logger
functions.description: Constructs a logger that wraps the provided implementation. The logger takes ownership of impl and will delete it. Throws if impl is null.
requirements: impl must be a non-null pointer; a null pointer will cause the constructor to throw (per documentation).
impl must be heap-allocated and remain valid until the logger takes ownership; after construction, the caller must not delete impl.
The provided impl must be a fully constructed soci::logger_impl (typically a derived class instance).

functions.name: soci::logger::logger
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a new logger as a copy of other, typically by cloning the underlying implementation so that both loggers manage independent implementations.
requirements: other must be a valid soci::logger instance.
Copies share no ownership of the same impl; behavior relies on proper clone support in the underlying implementation.

functions.name: soci::logger::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces this logger’s implementation with a copy of other’s implementation, typically via cloning, managing ownership appropriately.
requirements: other must be a valid soci::logger instance.
Self-assignment should be safely handled by the implementation.
Existing owned implementation (if any) will be released; no caller action required.

functions.name: soci::logger::~logger
functions.description: Destructor for soci::logger. Releases ownership and deletes the underlying implementation pointer.
requirements: The underlying impl must have been obtained via new (heap-allocated) so it can be safely deleted (ensured by construction requirements).
No further requirements for callers.

functions.name: soci::logger::start_query
functions.description: Forwards to the underlying implementation’s start_query() to record that a new query is about to execute.
requirements: Logger must have been constructed with a valid implementation (guaranteed by class invariants).
query may be any string; typically the SQL text.
Should be called before add_query_parameter() to associate parameters with this query (implied by documentation).

functions.name: soci::logger::add_query_parameter
functions.description: Forwards to the underlying implementation’s add_query_parameter() to log a parameter for the active query.
requirements: Call after start_query() to associate parameters with the current query (implied by documentation).
name and value may be empty; no explicit constraints.

functions.name: soci::logger::clear_query_parameters
functions.description: Forwards to the underlying implementation’s clear_query_parameters() to clear any logged parameters for the active query.
requirements: No explicit constraints; typically used when starting or finishing a query.

functions.name: soci::logger::set_stream
functions.description: Sets the output stream for basic session logging on the underlying implementation. Provided for compatibility with session::set_stream()-style APIs.
requirements: s may be nullptr to disable stream-based logging (implied).
Caller retains ownership of the stream; do not delete through the logger.

functions.name: soci::logger::get_stream
functions.description: Returns the current output stream configured in the underlying implementation for basic session logging, or nullptr if none.
requirements: May return nullptr if no stream is set.
Caller must not delete the returned stream; ownership is not transferred.

functions.name: soci::logger::get_last_query
functions.description: Returns the last query recorded by the underlying implementation, if supported.
requirements: May return an empty string if the implementation doesn’t track the last query.

functions.name: soci::logger::get_last_query_context
functions.description: Returns the last query’s context (e.g., parameters) from the underlying implementation, if supported.
requirements: May return an empty string if the implementation doesn’t track context or no parameters were recorded.

functions.name: soci::details::once_temp_type::once_temp_type
functions.description: Constructs a temporary, single-execution statement helper bound to the given session. Typically used via operator<< to accumulate SQL and bindings before executing once.
requirements: s must reference a valid, open soci::session for the entire lifetime of the once_temp_type instance.
The associated session must outlive this once_temp_type instance.

functions.name: soci::details::once_temp_type::operator=
functions.description: Assigns from another once_temp_type, sharing the underlying ref_counted_statement. Intended to remain lightweight and copyable.
requirements: The source object o must be a valid once_temp_type.
After assignment, both objects may reference the same underlying ref_counted_statement; do not rely on deep copy.

functions.name: soci::details::once_temp_type::~once_temp_type
functions.description: Destructor for once_temp_type. May perform cleanup on the associated statement and may throw.
requirements: Callers must be aware that this destructor can throw; avoid destroying once_temp_type during exception unwinding or in noexcept contexts where throwing would terminate the program.

functions.name: soci::details::once_temp_type::operator<<
functions.description: Accumulates SQL/text or statement components into the underlying statement builder and returns *this for chaining. Used to build a one-off statement before executing.
requirements: T must be a type supported by ref_counted_statement::accumulate(t); typically SQL fragments (e.g., std::string) or manipulators supported by SOCI.
The once_temp_type must be bound to a valid session (via its constructor) before use.

functions.name: soci::details::once_temp_type::operator,
functions.description: Binds an output (into) value to the statement being built, using SOCI's into_type_ptr binding. Enables chaining with the comma operator.
requirements: The provided soci::details::into_type_ptr must be a valid, initialized binding created by SOCI.
The once_temp_type must be associated with a valid session.
Use only with supported SOCI into bindings; unspecified behavior otherwise.

functions.name: soci::details::once_type::once_type
functions.description: Default-constructs a once_type with no associated session. Must set a session before use.
requirements: Before calling operator<< on this object, a valid session must be set via set_session(session*).

functions.name: soci::details::once_type::once_type
functions.description: Constructs a once_type bound to the provided session pointer, enabling creation of once_temp_type statements via operator<<.
requirements: s must be a valid, non-null pointer to an open soci::session that outlives any once_temp_type objects created from this once_type.

functions.name: soci::details::once_type::set_session
functions.description: Associates this once_type with a session to be used when creating one-off statements.
requirements: s must be a valid, non-null pointer to an open soci::session for subsequent use.
The provided session object must outlive subsequent uses of this once_type.

functions.name: soci::details::once_type::operator<<
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::once_temp_type soci::details::once_type::operator<<(T const & t)
functions.description: Creates a once_temp_type bound to the associated session, streams t into it, and returns the temporary for further chaining (e.g., bindings) and execution.
requirements: A valid, non-null session must have been set (via constructor or set_session) before calling this operator; otherwise dereferencing a null session pointer would occur.
T must be acceptable to once_temp_type::operator<<, i.e., supported by ref_counted_statement::accumulate.

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_type::prepare_type
functions.description: Default-constructs a prepare_type with no associated session. Must set a session before use.
requirements: Before calling operator<< on this object, a valid session must be set via set_session(session*).

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_type::prepare_type
functions.description: Constructs a prepare_type bound to the provided session pointer, enabling creation of prepared statements via operator<<.
requirements: s must be a valid, non-null pointer to an open soci::session that outlives any prepare_temp_type objects created from this prepare_type.

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_type::set_session
functions.description: Associates this prepare_type with a session to be used when creating prepared statements.
requirements: s must be a valid, non-null pointer to an open soci::session for subsequent use.
The provided session object must outlive subsequent uses of this prepare_type.

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_type::operator<<
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::prepare_temp_type soci::details::prepare_type::operator<<(T const & t)
functions.description: Creates a prepare_temp_type bound to the associated session, streams t into it, and returns it for further chaining (e.g., adding parameters) prior to preparing/executing.
requirements: A valid, non-null session must have been set (via constructor or set_session) before calling this operator.
T must be acceptable to prepare_temp_type::operator<< (i.e., ultimately to the underlying statement accumulation).

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::ddl_type
functions.description: Constructs a DDL builder/executor bound to the given session. Used to construct and execute DDL statements (create/alter/drop).
requirements: s must reference a valid, open soci::session that outlives this ddl_type instance.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::operator=
functions.description: Assigns from another ddl_type, sharing/pointing to the same underlying resources as appropriate.
requirements: d must be a valid ddl_type.
Post-assignment, internal state may be shared; do not rely on deep copy semantics.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::~ddl_type
functions.description: Destructor for ddl_type. May release underlying statement resources and may throw.
requirements: Callers must be aware that this destructor can throw; avoid destruction during exception unwinding or in noexcept-only contexts.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::create_table
functions.description: Begins or issues a CREATE TABLE DDL operation for the specified table name, using the internal builder/state.
requirements: tableName should be a valid, non-empty table identifier for the target database.
A valid session must be associated with this ddl_type (set by its constructor).

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::add_column
functions.signature: void soci::ddl_type::add_column(const std::string & tableName, const std::string & columnName, soci::db_type dt, int precision, int scale)
functions.description: Adds a column definition to a table (e.g., in an ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN or as part of a CREATE TABLE), specifying type and optional precision/scale.
requirements: tableName and columnName should be valid, non-empty identifiers.
dt must be a valid soci::db_type value understood by the backend.
precision and scale are expected to be non-negative integers when applicable to the type.
An associated valid session is required.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::add_column
functions.signature: void soci::ddl_type::add_column(const std::string & tableName, const std::string & columnName, soci::data_type dt, int precision, int scale)
functions.description: Deprecated overload that forwards to the db_type version. Adds a column of the given SOCI data_type.
requirements: tableName and columnName should be valid, non-empty identifiers.
dt must be a valid soci::data_type value.
precision and scale are expected to be non-negative integers when applicable.
An associated valid session is required.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::alter_column
functions.signature: void soci::ddl_type::alter_column(const std::string & tableName, const std::string & columnName, soci::db_type dt, int precision, int scale)
functions.description: Alters the definition of an existing column, changing its type and precision/scale as supported by the backend.
requirements: tableName and columnName should be valid, non-empty identifiers of an existing table/column.
dt must be a valid soci::db_type value.
precision and scale are expected to be non-negative integers when applicable.
An associated valid session is required.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::alter_column
functions.signature: void soci::ddl_type::alter_column(const std::string & tableName, const std::string & columnName, soci::data_type dt, int precision, int scale)
functions.description: Deprecated overload that forwards to the db_type version. Alters a column using SOCI data_type.
requirements: tableName and columnName should be valid, non-empty identifiers.
dt must be a valid soci::data_type value.
precision and scale are expected to be non-negative integers when applicable.
An associated valid session is required.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::drop_column
functions.signature: void soci::ddl_type::drop_column(const std::string & tableName, const std::string & columnName)
functions.description: Drops a column from the specified table.
requirements: tableName and columnName should be valid, non-empty identifiers.
Dropping columns must be supported by the backend; otherwise this may fail at runtime.
An associated valid session is required.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::column
functions.signature: soci::ddl_type & soci::ddl_type::column(const std::string & columnName, soci::db_type dt, int precision = 0, int scale = 0)
functions.description: Adds a column specification to the current DDL statement being built and returns *this for chaining.
requirements: columnName should be a valid, non-empty identifier.
dt must be a valid soci::db_type value.
precision and scale should be non-negative if used.
Use within the context of building a CREATE/ALTER statement with this object.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::column
functions.signature: soci::ddl_type & soci::ddl_type::column(const std::string & columnName, soci::data_type dt, int precision = 0, int scale = 0)
functions.description: Deprecated overload that forwards to the db_type version. Adds a column specification using SOCI data_type and returns *this for chaining.
requirements: columnName should be a valid, non-empty identifier.
dt must be a valid soci::data_type value.
precision and scale should be non-negative if used.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::unique
functions.signature: soci::ddl_type & soci::ddl_type::unique(const std::string & name, const std::string & columnNames)
functions.description: Adds a UNIQUE constraint definition with the given name on the specified column list and returns *this for chaining.
requirements: name should be a valid, non-empty constraint identifier.
columnNames should list one or more valid column identifiers in the format expected by the backend.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::primary_key
functions.signature: soci::ddl_type & soci::ddl_type::primary_key(const std::string & name, const std::string & columnNames)
functions.description: Adds a PRIMARY KEY constraint definition with the given name on the specified column list and returns *this for chaining.
requirements: name should be a valid, non-empty constraint identifier.
columnNames should list one or more valid column identifiers in the format expected by the backend.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::foreign_key
functions.signature: soci::ddl_type & soci::ddl_type::foreign_key(const std::string & name, const std::string & columnNames, const std::string & refTableName, const std::string & refColumnNames)
functions.description: Adds a FOREIGN KEY constraint definition with the given name from the specified columns to the referenced table/columns and returns *this for chaining.
requirements: name should be a valid, non-empty constraint identifier.
columnNames and refColumnNames should list valid column identifiers.
refTableName should be a valid, non-empty table identifier.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::operator()
functions.description: Appends an arbitrary SQL fragment to the DDL being built and returns *this for chaining. Allows issuing backend-specific clauses.
requirements: arbitrarySql should be a syntactically valid SQL fragment for the target backend.
Use with caution to ensure generated SQL remains valid.

functions.name: soci::ddl_type::set_tail
functions.description: Sets the delimiter or trailing text used between parts of DDL statements (e.g., commas, line breaks).
requirements: tail should be the desired delimiter/trailer string; must be valid for the intended SQL output.

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_temp_type::prepare_temp_type
functions.description: Constructor that initializes a lightweight, copyable builder for a prepared statement associated with the provided SOCI session. Typically used as the temporary object returned by session::prepare, then fed SQL fragments and bindings via operator<< and operator,.
requirements: sess must refer to a valid, initialized soci::session object.
The resulting prepare_temp_type object must be used according to SOCI’s prepare/execute workflow (details of execution are not shown here).

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_temp_type::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Assigns preparation state from another prepare_temp_type, enabling reuse of the builder. Expected to be safe for self-assignment.
requirements: other must be a valid prepare_temp_type instance.
The left-hand side object remains valid only if the usual object lifetime rules are respected (don’t use it after destruction).

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_temp_type::~prepare_temp_type
functions.description: Destructor. Releases the internal reference-counted preparation info used to accumulate SQL and bindings.
requirements: Do not access the object or any pointers obtained from get_prepare_info() after this destructor runs.

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_temp_type::operator<<
functions.description: Streams a fragment into the prepared statement builder. For supported T, this appends/accumulates SQL text or binding specifiers into the internal preparation info, and returns *this for chaining.
requirements: T must be a type accepted by ref_counted_prepare_info::accumulate(T const&).
The prepare_temp_type instance must be valid (not destroyed).

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_temp_type::operator,
functions.description: Comma operator overload that exchanges an output binding (into) with the builder. Enables syntax like pt << "..." , into(x).
requirements: i must be a valid into_type_ptr representing a prepared output binding.
The prepare_temp_type instance must be valid (not destroyed).

functions.name: soci::details::prepare_temp_type::get_prepare_info
functions.description: Returns the internal ref_counted_prepare_info pointer that holds the accumulated SQL and bindings for the prepared statement. Intended for internal use within SOCI.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid only as long as the originating prepare_temp_type (and any shared ownership) remains alive.
Caller must not delete or otherwise free the returned pointer.
Do not dereference the returned pointer after the prepare_temp_type is destroyed.

functions.name: soci::details::procedure_impl::procedure_impl
functions.description: Constructs a low-level procedure implementation object bound to the given database session. Initializes reference counting to 1 and forwards the session to the base statement_impl.
requirements: The soci::session reference must remain valid for at least as long as the created soci::details::procedure_impl object (the session is passed by reference and is expected to be used by the base class).

functions.name: soci::details::procedure_impl::inc_ref
functions.description: Increments the internal reference count for this procedure_impl instance. Used to manage shared ownership between wrapper objects.
requirements: Callers must ensure matching dec_ref() calls to balance increments to avoid leaks (inferred from reference counting semantics).

functions.name: soci::details::procedure_impl::dec_ref
functions.description: Decrements the internal reference count and deletes the object when the count reaches zero. Used to release shared ownership.
requirements: After dec_ref() causes deletion (i.e., when the count reaches zero), the caller must not access the object again (use-after-free risk).
The number of dec_ref() calls must not exceed the number of prior references (construction or inc_ref()) to avoid double-free (inferred from reference counting semantics).

functions.name: soci::procedure::procedure
functions.description: Conversion constructor that creates a high-level soci::procedure wrapper from a prepared temporary descriptor. Allocates a new soci::details::procedure_impl and initializes gotData_ to false.
requirements: prep must be a valid soci::details::prepare_temp_type produced by SOCI’s prepare API (exact structure unknown).
The underlying session/resources referenced by prep must remain valid for the lifetime of the created soci::procedure (inferred).

functions.name: soci::procedure::procedure
functions.description: Copy constructor. Shares the underlying procedure_impl with other via reference counting and copies the gotData_ flag.
requirements: other must be a valid soci::procedure instance.

functions.name: soci::procedure::~procedure
functions.description: Destructor for soci::procedure. Releases a reference to the underlying procedure_impl via dec_ref(), potentially deleting it.
requirements: The soci::procedure instance must not be used after destruction.
If other copies share the same implementation, they must not access it after all references are destroyed (standard ref-counting caveat).

functions.name: soci::procedure::operator=
functions.description: Assignment operator. Increments the reference count of other's implementation, decrements the current one (possibly deleting it), then shares other's implementation and copies gotData_.
requirements: Self-assignment is supported by the implementation sequence shown.
other must be a valid soci::procedure instance.
After assignment, previously held implementation may be deleted; callers must not hold external raw pointers to the old impl.

functions.name: soci::procedure::execute
functions.description: Executes the underlying stored procedure or statement. Forwards to the implementation’s execute() and records whether data was obtained.
requirements: The soci::procedure must have been constructed from a valid prepare_temp_type so that impl_ is non-null.
withDataExchange indicates whether data exchange is expected; exact semantics are backend-specific and not defined here (unknown details).
Check the returned bool to determine if data is available; subsequent logic should respect this.

functions.name: soci::procedure::fetch
functions.description: Fetches the next set of data from the procedure/statement, forwarding to the implementation’s fetch(). Updates and returns whether data was obtained.
requirements: The soci::procedure must refer to a valid implementation (i.e., created from a valid prepare_temp_type).
Typically called after execute() when more data may be available; exact sequencing semantics are not defined here (inferred/unknown).
Callers should use the returned bool to detect end-of-data.

functions.name: soci::procedure::got_data
functions.description: Returns whether the last execute() or fetch() call reported that data was obtained.
requirements: Only reflects the result of the most recent execute() or fetch() on this object.

functions.name: soci::details::query_transformation_function::~query_transformation_function
functions.description: Virtual destructor of the abstract base functor for SQL query transformations. Ensures proper cleanup via base-class pointers. Typical usage: delete objects of derived transformation types through soci::details::query_transformation_function*.
requirements: Object must be a valid instance (possibly of a derived class) when the destructor is invoked.
If used polymorphically, the base pointer must actually point to a complete derived object (standard C++ object lifetime requirement).

functions.name: soci::details::query_transformation_function::operator()
functions.description: Pure virtual call operator defining the interface for a string-to-string SQL query transformation. Implementations must take the input SQL as std::string and return a transformed std::string. Intended to be invoked just before executing an SQL statement.
requirements: Must be overridden by derived classes; this class is abstract.
Implementations must accept a const std::string& input and return a std::string result.
Implementations must be const-correct (not modifying observable state unless internally synchronized).
Callers must pass a valid std::string containing the SQL to transform.

functions.name: soci::details::query_transformation<T>::query_transformation
functions.description: Constructor that wraps a user-provided callable object into a query_transformation, adapting it to the query_transformation_function interface. The callable is stored by value and invoked to transform SQL strings.
requirements: Template parameter T must be CopyConstructible (stored by value internally).
Argument callback must be invocable as callback(std::string const&) and return a type convertible to std::string.
The provided callable should be valid for the lifetime of the query_transformation instance (copied into the instance).

functions.name: soci::details::query_transformation<T>::operator()
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
std::string operator()(std::string const& query) const override;
functions.description: Invokes the stored user-provided callable to transform the given SQL string and returns the transformed string. Used just before executing an SQL statement.
requirements: Parameter query must be a valid std::string containing the SQL to transform.
The stored callable T must remain a valid object (it is held by value) and be invocable with signature std::string(std::string const&) or return a type convertible to std::string.
Function does not specify exception guarantees; callers should be prepared for exceptions thrown by the user-provided callable.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_prepare_info::ref_counted_prepare_info
functions.description: Constructs a ref_counted_prepare_info helper associated with a SOCI session. This object collects bind/define information (use/into bindings) and statement text to be passed to a statement's constructor. Typical usage is internal to SOCI when preparing a statement; user code may see it indirectly via higher-level APIs.
requirements: Parameter s must reference a valid soci::session object.
The referenced session must remain valid for at least as long as the ref_counted_prepare_info instance exists.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_prepare_info::exchange
functions.description: Registers a single input binding ("use" binding) with this prepare-info object. Internally forwards the binding to the uses_ collection so it can be applied when the statement is constructed.
requirements: u must be a properly constructed use_type_ptr referring to a valid SOCI use binding object.
The referenced binding object must remain valid until the prepare-info is consumed to build the statement.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_prepare_info::final_action
functions.description: Lifecycle hook invoked after exchanges to finalize the prepare-info before it is used to construct/prepare a statement. Exact side effects are internal to SOCI; typically, it validates and seals the collected bindings and query text.
requirements: Intended to be called by SOCI internals; external callers generally should not invoke this directly.
No parameters; preconditions and postconditions are not specified in this header.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement_base::ref_counted_statement_base
functions.description: Constructs the base for reference-counted SOCI statements, storing a reference to the provided soci::session. Used by derived classes to build SQL text and ultimately execute a statement when the reference count reaches zero.
requirements: Parameter s must refer to a valid soci::session object.
The referenced soci::session must outlive this ref_counted_statement_base instance (the session is stored by reference).

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement_base::~ref_counted_statement_base
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the reference-counted statement base. Enables safe destruction through base pointers.
requirements: Object must not already have been destroyed (do not access the object after dec_ref() causes deletion).

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement_base::final_action
functions.description: Pure virtual hook that derived classes implement to perform the final action when the reference count drops to zero (e.g., execute the built statement). Called by dec_ref() after any pending tail text is accumulated.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes.
Implementations should be prepared to be called exactly once from dec_ref() when the reference count reaches zero.
Exceptions thrown will be propagated after the object is deleted (dec_ref() catches, deletes this, then rethrows).

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement_base::inc_ref
functions.description: Increments the internal reference count for this statement object.
requirements: Each call to inc_ref() should be balanced by a corresponding call to dec_ref().
Not thread-safe unless external synchronization is provided.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement_base::dec_ref
functions.description: Decrements the internal reference count; when it reaches zero, appends any queued tail SQL text and invokes final_action(), then deletes this object. If final_action() throws, the object is still deleted and the exception is rethrown.
requirements: For the final decrement to zero, the caller must not access the object after this call (the object deletes itself).
Objects must be heap-allocated (not on the stack or embedded) because dec_ref() will execute 'delete this'.
Each previous inc_ref() must be matched by a dec_ref().
Not thread-safe unless external synchronization is provided.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement_base::accumulate
functions.description: Appends the provided value to the internal SQL text stream used to build the statement. Typically used to incrementally construct a query.
requirements: Type T must be stream-insertable into std::ostringstream via operator<<(std::ostringstream&, T) or an equivalent overload.
Must not be called after dec_ref() has deleted the object.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement_base::set_tail
functions.description: Sets trailing SQL/text to be appended to the built query just before the final action is performed when the reference count reaches zero.
requirements: tail may be any string; it will be appended if non-empty when dec_ref() performs the final action.
Must not be called after dec_ref() has deleted the object.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement_base::set_need_comma
functions.description: Sets an internal flag indicating whether a comma is needed when generating portable DDL or composite SQL fragments.
requirements: No specific value constraints; boolean flag controls formatting logic in derived code.
Must not be called after dec_ref() has deleted the object.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement_base::get_need_comma
functions.description: Returns the current state of the 'need comma' formatting flag used during SQL generation.
requirements: Object must be alive (not yet deleted via dec_ref()).

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement::ref_counted_statement
functions.description: Constructs a reference-counted 'once' statement wrapper bound to the given session. Uses the base to build SQL and holds an internal soci::statement to execute.
requirements: Parameter s must refer to a valid soci::session object.
The soci::session referenced must outlive this ref_counted_statement instance.

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement::final_action
functions.description: Overrides the base hook to perform the final action for 'once' statements. Based on class comments, this executes the accumulated statement when the reference count drops to zero. Exact behavior is defined in the implementation (.cpp).
requirements: May be called exactly once by dec_ref() when the reference count reaches zero.
Any resources or bound data required for execution must still be valid at this time (inferred from SOCI execution patterns).

functions.name: soci::details::ref_counted_statement::exchange
functions.description: Forwards an exchange (binding) to the underlying soci::statement, allowing use/into bindings to be associated with the statement before execution.
requirements: Type T must be compatible with soci::statement::exchange (e.g., SOCI use/into/exchange types).
The object referenced by t must remain valid until the statement is executed by final_action() (inferred from typical SOCI binding semantics).
Must be called before the final execution triggered by dec_ref().

functions.name: soci::details::into_type<row>::into_type
functions.description: Constructs an into_type binding for SOCI that directs a statement to fetch result rows into the provided soci::row instance (dynamic row binding). Intended to be used internally by SOCI when users write into(row) for dynamic queries. The constructor stores a reference to r; during statement definition, the row is registered via statement_impl::set_row, and on fetch the row is populated and its get counter reset.
requirements: r must be a valid soci::row lvalue that remains alive for the entire lifetime of the into_type object and at least until the associated statement finishes execution/fetching, because the constructor stores and later uses a reference to it.
r must be in a state acceptable to be filled by SOCI (typically default-constructed soci::row).
No error is reported by the constructor; lifetime and usage errors (e.g., dangling reference) are the caller’s responsibility.

functions.name: soci::details::into_type<row>::into_type
functions.description: Same as the single-argument constructor, but accepts an indicator reference for API symmetry with other into bindings. For row, the indicator parameter is ignored; the row itself is used as the target for fetched data in dynamic queries.
requirements: r must be a valid soci::row lvalue that remains alive for the entire lifetime of the into_type object and at least until the associated statement finishes execution/fetching, because the constructor stores and later uses a reference to it.
The indicator argument must be a valid lvalue (non-temporary) of type soci::indicator, but its value is not used or modified by this specialization.
No error is reported by the constructor; lifetime and usage errors (e.g., dangling reference) are the caller’s responsibility.

functions.description: Sets the legacy SOCI data_type for the column. Deprecated: prefer set_db_type(db_type).

functions.name: soci::column_properties::set_db_type
functions.description: Sets the SOCI db_type (database/native type mapping) for the column.

functions.name: soci::row::row
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty row, ready to have column properties and value holders added by SOCI's result fetching mechanisms.

functions.description: Destructs the row and releases its resources/holders.

functions.description: Move-assigns from another row, transferring ownership of internal resources.

functions.name: soci::row::uppercase_column_names

functions.name: soci::row::clean_up
functions.description: Resets/cleans the row’s internal state and resources. Intended to clear holders/indicators so the row can be reused. Exact effects depend on the implementation; details not shown in this header.

functions.name: soci::row::get_indicator
functions.description: Returns the indicator (e.g., i_ok, i_null) for the column at the given index.
requirements: pos must be less than size(); otherwise an out-of-range exception will be thrown when accessing the internal container.

functions.name: soci::row::get_properties
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the column properties at the given index (name and type info).
requirements: pos must be less than size(); otherwise an out-of-range exception will be thrown.

functions.name: soci::row::get
functions.signature: template <typename T> T soci::row::get(std::size_t pos) const
functions.description: Converts and returns the value of the column at pos as type T using soci::type_conversion<T>. Throws if pos is invalid or if conversion fails.
requirements: pos must be less than size().
T must have a valid soci::type_conversion<T> specialization.
T must be convertible/copy-assignable from type_conversion<T>::base_type (per static_assert in the implementation).
The column at pos must not be null; to handle nulls, use the overload with a nullValue parameter.

functions.name: soci::row::move_as
functions.signature: template <typename T> T soci::row::move_as(std::size_t pos) const
functions.description: Moves the value of the column at pos into a T using soci::type_conversion<T>::move_from_base, allowing move semantics from the base value. After moving, the internal base value is reset to a default-constructed T-compatible state.
requirements: pos must be less than size().
T must have a valid soci::type_conversion<T> specialization.
T must be constructible from an rvalue of type type_conversion<T>::base_type (per static_assert).
The column must not be null; to handle nulls, use the overload with a nullValue parameter.

functions.name: soci::row::move_as
functions.signature: template <typename T> T soci::row::move_as(std::size_t pos, T const& nullValue) const
functions.description: Returns nullValue if the column at pos is NULL; otherwise moves the column value into a T using type_conversion<T>::move_from_base.
requirements: pos must be less than size().
T must have a valid soci::type_conversion<T> specialization and be constructible from base_type rvalue.

functions.name: soci::row::operator>>
functions.signature: template <typename T> soci::row const& soci::row::operator>>(T& value) const
functions.description: Sequential extractor: assigns value from the current column (currentPos_) converted to T, then advances the internal position. Enables chained extraction like row >> a >> b.
requirements: currentPos_ must be less than size(); otherwise extraction will throw due to out-of-range access.
T must have a valid soci::type_conversion<T> specialization and satisfy copy-assignability from base_type.
The current column must not be null; to handle nulls, use get with a nullValue or check the indicator first.

functions.name: soci::row::skip
functions.description: Advances the internal extraction position by num columns without reading values, for use with operator>> style iteration.

functions.name: soci::row::reset_get_counter
functions.description: Resets the internal extraction position (currentPos_) to the beginning of the row for subsequent operator>> operations.

functions.name: soci::rowid::rowid
functions.description: Constructs a rowid object that provides backend-specific ROWID support associated with a given soci::session. Typical usage is to create a rowid tied to an active database session so it can be bound to statements that operate on database ROWID values. Internal details are backend-specific and not visible here; exact behavior depends on the connected backend. Some details (such as lifetime coupling to the session) are not documented in this header and remain unknown.
requirements: Parameter s must reference a valid soci::session object that has been properly initialized/opened for use.
The function is explicit; callers must not rely on implicit conversions when constructing soci::rowid.
Thread-safety and exception behavior are not documented in this header (unknown).

functions.name: soci::rowid::~rowid
functions.description: Destructor for soci::rowid. Releases any backend-specific resources associated with the rowid instance. Intended to clean up the underlying implementation when the wrapper goes out of scope.
requirements: After destruction, the soci::rowid instance must not be used.
Callers must not attempt to manually delete or free the underlying backend object returned by get_backend(); ownership is managed by soci::rowid.
Exception behavior during destruction is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: soci::rowid::get_backend
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the backend-specific rowid implementation object. Primarily intended for SOCI backend/internal code to access database-driver-specific functionality for ROWID handling. Not typically used by end-user code. The returned pointer reflects the current state of this rowid object.
requirements: The soci::rowid instance must be properly constructed before calling get_backend().
The returned pointer must not be deleted or otherwise freed by the caller; ownership is retained by soci::rowid.
The returned pointer may be null (not documented here), so callers should check for null before dereferencing (inferred from raw pointer return).
The pointer is only valid while the soci::rowid object remains alive; do not retain or use it after the rowid is destroyed.
Thread-safety of accessing the backend pointer is not documented (unknown).

functions.name: soci::rowset_iterator::operator*
functions.description: Returns a reference to the current element bound to this input iterator. Typically used to access the current row/object extracted from the underlying SOCI statement. Only valid when the iterator is dereferenceable (i.e., not the end iterator).
requirements: The iterator must not be at end; it must refer to a valid element (st_ and define_ must be non-null).
Dereferencing an end iterator is undefined and will likely crash.

functions.name: soci::rowset_iterator::operator->
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current element for member access syntax (it simply returns the address of operator*()). Only valid when the iterator is dereferenceable.
requirements: The iterator must not be at end; it must refer to a valid element (st_ and define_ must be non-null).
Using operator-> on an end iterator is undefined and will likely crash.

functions.name: soci::rowset_iterator::operator++
functions.description: Pre-increment. Advances the input iterator to the next row by fetching from the underlying statement. If no more rows are available, the iterator becomes the end iterator (non-dereferenceable).
requirements: The iterator must not be at end when called; st_ must be non-null.
After advancing past the last row, the iterator becomes an end iterator and must not be dereferenced.
This is a single-pass input iterator; copying and incrementing copies independently may not behave as multi-pass iterators.

functions.name: soci::rowset_iterator::operator++
functions.description: Post-increment. Returns a copy of the iterator prior to advancing, then advances this iterator to the next row. If no more rows are available, this iterator becomes the end iterator.
requirements: The iterator must not be at end when called; st_ must be non-null.
Returned temporary may still be dereferenceable if there was a current element; after increment, this iterator may become end and must not be dereferenced.
This is a single-pass input iterator; do not assume multi-pass semantics.

functions.name: soci::rowset_iterator::operator==
functions.description: Compares two rowset input iterators for equality by comparing their underlying statement and bound object pointers. End iterators compare equal to each other.
requirements: No special preconditions; it is safe to compare any two rowset_iterators of the same T type.
Iterators that refer to different underlying statements/rowsets will compare unequal.

functions.name: soci::rowset_iterator::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality comparison for rowset input iterators; logical negation of operator==.
requirements: No special preconditions; it is safe to compare any two rowset_iterators of the same T type.

functions.name: soci::details::rowset_impl::incRef
functions.description: Increments the reference count of the rowset implementation. Used internally by soci::rowset to manage shared ownership of the implementation object.
requirements: Each successful incRef() should eventually be balanced by a corresponding decRef() to avoid memory leaks.
Thread-safety is not specified; external synchronization may be required if used across threads.

functions.name: soci::details::rowset_impl::decRef
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of the rowset implementation and deletes the object when the count reaches zero. Used internally by soci::rowset to manage lifetime.
requirements: Must only be called to balance a prior incRef() on the same object.
After decRef() deletes the object (when the count reaches zero), the caller must not access the object again (use-after-free risk).
Thread-safety is not specified; external synchronization may be required if used across threads.

functions.name: soci::details::rowset_impl::begin
functions.description: Returns an input iterator positioned at the first row of the result set. If the rowset is empty or uninitialized, returns an end iterator. No ownership is transferred.
requirements: The returned iterator is a single-pass input iterator; algorithms must not assume multi-pass behavior.
Dereferencing the returned iterator is only valid if it is not equal to end().
For empty or uninitialized rowsets, begin() equals end().

functions.name: soci::details::rowset_impl::end
functions.description: Returns the end iterator for the rowset (a non-dereferenceable sentinel).
requirements: Never dereference the end iterator.
Use only for comparisons to detect the end of iteration.

functions.name: soci::rowset::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment. Shares the underlying implementation with rhs by increasing its reference count, releases the current implementation (possibly deleting it), and assigns the shared pointer to this rowset.
requirements: Self-assignment is handled; no special action required by caller.
Any iterators obtained from this rowset prior to assignment are invalidated and must not be used after assignment.
After assignment, both rowsets share the same underlying implementation; modifying one affects iterator validity for both.

functions.name: soci::rowset::clear
functions.description: Resets this rowset to an empty state by assigning a default-constructed implementation. Effectively releases the current implementation and any associated resources.
requirements: Any iterators obtained from this rowset prior to clear() are invalidated and must not be used afterwards.

functions.name: soci::rowset::begin
functions.description: Returns a const input iterator to the first element (row) in the rowset, or the end iterator if the rowset is empty or uninitialized.
requirements: The returned iterator is single-pass; do not assume multi-pass semantics.
Dereference only if iterator != end().

functions.name: soci::rowset::end
functions.description: Returns the const end iterator for this rowset (a non-dereferenceable sentinel).
requirements: Never dereference the end iterator.
Use only for comparisons against iterators returned by begin().
