functions.name: soci::session::get_last_insert_id
functions.signature: bool soci::session::get_last_insert_id(std::string const & table, long long & value)
functions.description: Retrieves the last auto-generated value for the specified table in this session. Some backends ignore the table argument and return the last auto-generated value overall. Returns true on success and sets value.
requirements: table should identify a target table (semantics may be backend-specific).
value is an output parameter that will be assigned when the function returns true.
A working connection must exist.

functions.name: soci::session::get_table_names
functions.description: Returns a once_temp_type representing an internally composed query that lists table names in the current schema. Typically bind a std::vector<std::string> to fetch all results at once.
requirements: Use with once-style execution; bind a container (e.g., std::vector<std::string>) to collect multiple results, as the query usually returns multiple rows.

functions.name: soci::session::prepare_table_names
functions.description: Returns a prepare_temp_type for an internally composed query listing table names in the current schema. Intended for use with statement objects to fetch rows sequentially (e.g., bind std::string for the single output field).
requirements: Use with prepared statements; fetch results one row at a time, binding a std::string for the output field.

functions.name: soci::session::prepare_column_descriptions
functions.description: Returns a prepare_temp_type for an internally composed query listing column descriptions for the specified table. The argument is non-const to prevent temporaries and is bound as a regular "use" element. The table_name can include an optional schema (schema.table).
requirements: table_name must be an lvalue std::string that remains valid for the lifetime of the prepared statement/bindings.
table_name may include schema and table separated by a dot.

functions.name: soci::session::create_table
functions.description: Begins building a portable DDL statement for creating a table with the given name. Returns a ddl_type builder object.
requirements: tableName should be a valid table identifier for the target backend.
Follow-up calls on ddl_type are required to define columns before execution (details depend on ddl_type; not specified here).

functions.name: soci::session::drop_table
functions.description: Drops a table with the given name in a portable way, if supported by the backend.
requirements: tableName should identify an existing table (backend-dependent behavior on non-existent tables is not specified).
A working connection must exist.

functions.name: soci::session::truncate_table
functions.description: Truncates (empties) the specified table in a portable way, if supported by the backend.
requirements: tableName should identify an existing table.
A working connection must exist.

functions.name: soci::session::add_column
functions.signature: soci::ddl_type soci::session::add_column(std::string const & tableName, std::string const & columnName, soci::db_type dt, int precision = 0, int scale = 0)
functions.description: Begins building a portable DDL statement to add a column to a table with the specified type and optional precision/scale.
requirements: tableName and columnName should be valid identifiers for the target backend.
dt must be a valid soci::db_type.
precision and scale apply to numeric types as per backend rules.

functions.name: soci::session::alter_column
functions.signature: soci::ddl_type soci::session::alter_column(std::string const & tableName, std::string const & columnName, soci::db_type dt, int precision = 0, int scale = 0)
functions.description: Begins building a portable DDL statement to alter a column's type and optional precision/scale.
requirements: tableName and columnName should be valid identifiers.
dt must be a valid soci::db_type.
precision and scale semantics are backend-specific.

functions.name: soci::session::drop_column
functions.signature: soci::ddl_type soci::session::drop_column(std::string const & tableName, std::string const & columnName)
functions.description: Begins building a portable DDL statement to drop a column from a table.
requirements: tableName and columnName should be valid identifiers for the target backend.

functions.name: soci::session::empty_blob
functions.description: Returns a backend-specific SQL fragment representing an empty BLOB value.
requirements: Exact returned syntax is backend-specific and not detailed here.

functions.name: soci::session::nvl
functions.description: Returns a backend-specific SQL function name or fragment for NULL value substitution (NVL/COALESCE equivalent).
requirements: Exact returned syntax/name is backend-specific and not detailed here.

functions.name: soci::session::get_dummy_from_table
functions.description: Returns the name of a dummy table required in FROM clauses for SELECTs without real tables (e.g., "DUAL" for Oracle). Returns an empty string if not needed by the backend.

functions.name: soci::session::get_dummy_from_clause
functions.description: Returns a possibly empty FROM clause (including leading space) for SELECTs without real tables (e.g., " FROM DUAL").

functions.name: soci::session::set_failover_callback
functions.description: Sets the failover callback object to be used when the connection fails over to another node/connection.
requirements: callback must be a valid soci::failover_callback instance. Lifetime/ownership requirements are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: soci::session::get_backend
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the underlying backend-specific session object for diagnostics and advanced use (intended to be downcast to the concrete backend type).
requirements: Pointer may be null if no backend is associated/open (not explicitly documented; unknown).
Caller is responsible for safe downcasting and must not delete the returned pointer.

functions.name: soci::session::get_backend_name
functions.description: Returns the name of the currently used backend.

functions.name: soci::session::make_statement_backend
functions.description: Creates and returns a backend-specific statement object associated with this session.
requirements: Returned pointer ownership and lifetime management are backend/SOCI-internal; caller must follow SOCI usage patterns and not delete it directly (exact policy not specified here).
A working connection must exist.

functions.name: soci::session::make_rowid_backend
functions.description: Creates and returns a backend-specific rowid object associated with this session.
requirements: Returned pointer ownership/lifetime are SOCI-internal; caller must not delete directly (policy not specified here).
A working connection must exist.

functions.name: soci::session::make_blob_backend
functions.description: Creates and returns a backend-specific BLOB object associated with this session.
requirements: Returned pointer ownership/lifetime are SOCI-internal; caller must not delete directly (policy not specified here).
A working connection must exist.

functions.name: soci::details::to_db_type
functions.description: Converts a legacy soci::data_type value to the corresponding soci::db_type. Used to map deprecated data_type to the newer db_type enum.
requirements: dt must be one of the soci::data_type enumerators (dt_string, dt_date, dt_double, dt_integer, dt_long_long, dt_unsigned_long_long, dt_blob, dt_xml).

functions.name: soci::details::standard_into_type_backend::define_by_pos
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::standard_into_type_backend::define_by_pos(int& position, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type) = 0
functions.description: Binds an output ("into") value at the given positional index to receive data of the specified exchange_type during fetch. Implemented by backends.
requirements: position is an in/out 1-based position; on success it is advanced to the next bind slot as per backend convention (inferred from SOCI patterns).
data must point to a buffer/object compatible with the provided exchange_type.
Must be called before executing/fetching the statement.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_into_type_backend::pre_exec
functions.description: Optional hook invoked before statement execution. Default implementation does nothing. Backends may use it to prepare buffers for the next execution (single or bulk).
requirements: If overridden by a backend, caller may pass num as the number of rows to execute in bulk; semantics backend-defined.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_into_type_backend::pre_fetch
functions.description: Hook called before fetching rows. Allows the backend to prepare the bound into buffers.
requirements: Must be called by the statement before fetching; caller must ensure prior successful define_by_pos.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_into_type_backend::post_fetch
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::standard_into_type_backend::post_fetch(bool gotData, bool calledFromFetch, soci::indicator* ind) = 0
functions.description: Hook called after fetching rows. Backend writes indicator state (null/ok/truncated) and may finalize value conversions.
requirements: ind must be a valid pointer to an indicator variable provided by the caller.
gotData indicates whether data was retrieved; calledFromFetch indicates context; semantics backend-defined but must be consistent with SOCI usage.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_into_type_backend::clean_up
functions.description: Releases any resources associated with this into binding.
requirements: Must be called when the binding is no longer needed (typically on statement cleanup).
May be called once; further calls are backend-defined.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::define_by_pos_bulk
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::define_by_pos_bulk(int& position, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type, std::size_t begin, std::size_t* end)
functions.description: Attempts to bind a bulk (iterator-range) vector "into" buffer. Default implementation throws soci_error indicating unsupported feature for the backend.
requirements: By default, calling this function will throw soci_error("into bulk iterators are not supported with this backend").
If a backend overrides it, data must reference a contiguous container compatible with type; begin/end denote the range; end must be a valid pointer where backend may write the effective end index.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::define_by_pos
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::define_by_pos(int& position, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type) = 0
functions.description: Binds a vector output buffer at the given position for bulk fetching according to the exchange_type.
requirements: position is 1-based in/out; data must point to a compatible std::vector-like storage for the given type.
Must be called before fetching.
The vector size must be set (via resize) before fetch.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::pre_exec
functions.description: Optional hook before execution for vector into bindings. Default does nothing.
requirements: If overridden, num may indicate the number of rows to execute; backend-defined semantics.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::pre_fetch
functions.description: Hook called before fetching rows into vector buffers.
requirements: Caller must have bound the vector via define_by_pos and sized it appropriately via resize().

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::post_fetch
functions.description: Hook called after fetching rows in bulk into the vector. Backend updates indicators per-row as needed.
requirements: ind must point to an array/buffer of indicator values sized to the vector length when required by the backend.
gotData indicates whether any rows were fetched.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::resize
functions.description: Resizes the underlying vector buffer to hold up to sz rows.
requirements: sz must be a valid size for the underlying container type.
Should be called before fetch.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::size
functions.description: Returns the current size (capacity in rows) of the bound vector buffer.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_into_type_backend::clean_up
functions.description: Releases resources for a vector into binding.
requirements: Must be called during statement/binding cleanup.
Multiple calls behavior is backend-defined.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::standard_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos(int& position, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type, bool readOnly) = 0
functions.description: Binds an input ("use") value at the given positional index with the specified exchange_type. readOnly hints whether the backend may modify the buffer.
requirements: position is 1-based in/out; data must point to a buffer/object compatible with exchange_type.
Must be called before execution.
If readOnly is false, backend may write-back (e.g., for OUT parameters).

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type_backend::bind_by_name
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::standard_use_type_backend::bind_by_name(const std::string& name, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type, bool readOnly) = 0
functions.description: Binds an input ("use") value by parameter name with the given exchange_type. readOnly controls whether the backend can modify the value (for INOUT/OUT).
requirements: name must match a parameter placeholder recognized by the backend.
data must be compatible with exchange_type.
Must be called before execution.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type_backend::pre_exec
functions.description: Optional hook invoked before statement execution for scalar use bindings. Default does nothing.
requirements: If overridden, num may indicate number of rows for bulk execution; semantics backend-defined.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type_backend::pre_use
functions.description: Hook called before executing a statement to prepare the use-bound value and its indicator (e.g., null handling).
requirements: ind must point to a valid indicator for the bound value or be nullptr if not used; backend semantics define how nulls are signaled.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type_backend::post_use
functions.description: Hook called after execution; used for OUT/INOUT parameters to transfer values back and set indicators.
requirements: ind must be a valid pointer if OUT/INOUT semantics are used.
gotData indicates whether the execution produced results affecting this parameter; semantics backend-defined.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type_backend::clean_up
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a scalar use binding.
requirements: Call during statement cleanup to avoid leaks.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos(int& position, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type) = 0
functions.description: Binds a vector of input values at the given positional index for bulk execution.
requirements: position is 1-based in/out; data must reference a vector-like container compatible with exchange_type.
Must be called before execution; container size controls number of rows to execute.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos_bulk
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos_bulk(int& position, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type, std::size_t begin, std::size_t* end)
functions.description: Attempts to bind a subrange (iterator-style) of a bulk input vector by position. Default implementation throws soci_error indicating unsupported feature.
requirements: By default, calling this function throws soci_error("using bulk iterators are not supported with this backend").
If overridden, begin/end specify the subrange; end must be a valid pointer to receive the effective end index; data must be compatible with type.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_name
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_name(const std::string& name, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type) = 0
functions.description: Binds a vector of input values by name for bulk execution.
requirements: name must match a backend parameter placeholder.
data must reference a vector-like container compatible with exchange_type.
Must be called before execution.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_name_bulk
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_name_bulk(const std::string& name, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type, std::size_t begin, std::size_t* end)
functions.description: Attempts to bind a subrange (iterator-style) of a bulk input vector by name. Default implementation throws soci_error indicating unsupported feature.
requirements: By default, calling this function throws soci_error("using bulk iterators are not supported with this backend").
If overridden by a backend, begin/end specify the subrange; end must be a valid pointer; data must be compatible with type.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::pre_exec
functions.description: Optional hook invoked before executing a statement with vector use bindings. Default does nothing.
requirements: If overridden, num may indicate planned number of rows; semantics backend-defined.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::pre_use
functions.description: Hook called before execution to prepare vector use bindings, using an optional array of indicators.
requirements: ind, if non-null, must point to an array of indicators with at least size() elements.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::size
functions.description: Returns the number of elements (rows) in the bound vector input buffer.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type_backend::clean_up
functions.description: Releases resources for a vector use binding.
requirements: Call during statement cleanup.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::alloc
functions.description: Allocates backend-specific statement resources/handles.
requirements: Must be called before prepare/execute/fetch as required by the backend lifecycle.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::clean_up
functions.description: Releases backend-specific statement resources/handles and any associated bindings.
requirements: Should be called when the statement is no longer needed.
Must not be used after cleanup.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::prepare
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::statement_backend::prepare(const std::string& query, soci::details::statement_type eType) = 0
functions.description: Prepares the SQL text for execution. statement_type can hint optimization (one-time vs repeatable).
requirements: query must contain valid SQL for the backend.
Must be called before execute() for prepared statements.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::execute
functions.description: Executes the prepared statement or one-shot query. For bulk operations, number can indicate the number of rows to process.
requirements: number should be >= 1 for execution; semantics may vary per backend.
Returns ef_success or ef_no_data to signal if data is available.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::fetch
functions.description: Fetches the next batch of rows after execution. number typically indicates the maximum number of rows to fetch.
requirements: Must be preceded by execute() when fetching from a query.
number should be >= 1; semantics backend-defined.
Returns ef_success if rows were fetched, ef_no_data if result set exhausted.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::get_affected_rows
functions.description: Returns the number of rows affected by the last DML operation for this statement.
requirements: Valid after execute() of a DML statement; value backend-defined for queries.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::get_number_of_rows
functions.description: Returns the number of rows fetched in the last fetch() call.
requirements: Call after fetch() to obtain the count for the last batch.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::get_parameter_name
functions.description: Returns the backend-specific name for the bind parameter at the given index, if supported.
requirements: index refers to the parameter position starting at 1 in most backends (inferred from SOCI patterns).

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::get_row_to_dump
functions.description: Returns the index of a row of interest for diagnostic dumps (e.g., the first row that caused an error) or -1 if not applicable. Default returns -1.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::rewrite_for_procedure_call
functions.description: Rewrites a query string into a backend-specific procedure call syntax when needed.
requirements: query should be a procedure call in a portable SOCI form.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::prepare_for_describe
functions.description: Prepares the statement for column description and returns the number of columns.
requirements: Call before describe_column() to initialize metadata access.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::describe_column
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::statement_backend::describe_column(int colNum, soci::db_type& dbtype, std::string& column_name) = 0
functions.description: Retrieves metadata for a column: deduced db_type and column name for the specified 1-based column index.
requirements: colNum must be within [1, number_of_columns].
dbtype and column_name must be writable references to receive results.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::to_data_type
functions.description: Maps a deduced soci::db_type to the legacy soci::data_type used by older SOCI APIs. Default implementation provides a consistent mapping.
requirements: dbt must be a valid soci::db_type value.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::make_into_type_backend
functions.description: Factory method to create a backend-specific standard_into_type_backend for scalar outputs.
requirements: Caller takes ownership per backend contract; must delete via clean_up/appropriate deleter when done.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::make_use_type_backend
functions.description: Factory method to create a backend-specific standard_use_type_backend for scalar inputs.
requirements: Caller must manage the lifetime according to backend rules.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::make_vector_into_type_backend
functions.description: Factory method to create a backend-specific vector_into_type_backend for bulk outputs.
requirements: Caller must manage the lifetime appropriately.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::make_vector_use_type_backend
functions.description: Factory method to create a backend-specific vector_use_type_backend for bulk inputs.
requirements: Caller must manage the lifetime appropriately.

functions.name: soci::details::statement_backend::exchange_dbtype_for
functions.description: Allows a backend to adjust the db_type used for fetching to account for backend-specific type deduction quirks. Default returns the input type unchanged.
requirements: type must be a valid soci::db_type.

functions.name: soci::details::blob_backend::get_len
functions.description: Returns the current length of the BLOB in bytes.

functions.name: soci::details::blob_backend::read_from_start
functions.signature: virtual std::size_t soci::details::blob_backend::read_from_start(void* buf, std::size_t toRead, std::size_t offset) = 0
functions.description: Reads up to toRead bytes from the BLOB starting at absolute offset (from start) into buf. Returns the number of bytes actually read.
requirements: buf must point to a valid writable memory region of at least toRead bytes when toRead > 0.
Offset is zero-based from the start of the BLOB.
Behavior when reading past EOF should be to read fewer bytes (backend-defined).

functions.name: soci::details::blob_backend::write_from_start
functions.signature: virtual std::size_t soci::details::blob_backend::write_from_start(const void* buf, std::size_t toWrite, std::size_t offset) = 0
functions.description: Writes up to toWrite bytes from buf into the BLOB starting at absolute offset from start. Returns the number of bytes actually written.
requirements: buf must point to a readable memory region of at least toWrite bytes when toWrite > 0.
Offset is zero-based from the start of the BLOB.

functions.name: soci::details::blob_backend::append
functions.signature: virtual std::size_t soci::details::blob_backend::append(const void* buf, std::size_t toWrite) = 0
functions.description: Appends up to toWrite bytes from buf to the end of the BLOB. Returns the number of bytes appended.
requirements: buf must point to a readable memory region of at least toWrite bytes when toWrite > 0.

functions.name: soci::details::blob_backend::trim
functions.description: Truncates or extends the BLOB to newLen bytes (extension semantics backend-defined; many backends only support truncation).
requirements: newLen must be within the limits supported by the backend.

functions.name: soci::details::blob_backend::get_session_backend
functions.description: Returns the session_backend associated with this BLOB for issuing backend-specific operations.
requirements: The returned reference must remain valid as long as the blob_backend exists.

functions.name: soci::details::blob_backend::read
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::details::blob_backend::read(std::size_t offset, void* buf, std::size_t toRead)
functions.description: Deprecated compatibility method to read from the BLOB. By default forwards to read_from_start(buf, toRead, offset) or backend-specific deprecated implementation.
requirements: buf must be a valid writable buffer of at least toRead bytes when toRead > 0.
Offset is zero-based from the start of the BLOB.
Callers should prefer read_from_start().

functions.name: soci::details::blob_backend::write
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::details::blob_backend::write(std::size_t offset, const void* buf, std::size_t toWrite)
functions.description: Deprecated compatibility method to write to the BLOB. By default forwards to write_from_start(buf, toWrite, offset) or backend-specific deprecated implementation.
requirements: buf must be a readable buffer of at least toWrite bytes when toWrite > 0.
Offset is zero-based from the start of the BLOB.
Callers should prefer write_from_start().

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::is_connected
functions.description: Returns true if the session is currently connected to the database.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::begin
functions.description: Begins a transaction on the session.
requirements: Session must be connected.
Nested transaction support is backend-defined.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::commit
functions.description: Commits the current transaction.
requirements: A transaction must be active as required by the backend.
Session must be connected.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::rollback
functions.description: Rolls back the current transaction.
requirements: A transaction must be active as required by the backend.
Session must be connected.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::get_next_sequence_value
functions.signature: virtual bool soci::details::session_backend::get_next_sequence_value(soci::session& , const std::string& , long long& )
functions.description: Retrieves the next value from a named database sequence into the provided reference. Default implementation returns false (unsupported).
requirements: Parameters: session&, sequence name, output long long reference.
Returns true if value was obtained; false if unsupported or not available.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::get_last_insert_id
functions.signature: virtual bool soci::details::session_backend::get_last_insert_id(soci::session& , const std::string& , long long& )
functions.description: Retrieves the last auto-generated ID for the given table/object name into the provided reference. Default implementation returns false (unsupported).
requirements: Parameters: session&, table/object name, output long long reference.
Returns true if value was obtained; false if unsupported or not available.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::get_table_names_query
functions.description: Returns a backend-specific SQL query (no parameters) that lists table names in the current schema. Default returns a PostgreSQL-flavored INFORMATION_SCHEMA query for 'public'.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::get_column_descriptions_query
functions.description: Returns a backend-specific SQL query (with one parameter :t) that lists column metadata for a table. Default returns a PostgreSQL-flavored INFORMATION_SCHEMA query.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::create_table
functions.description: Returns the beginning of a CREATE TABLE statement for the backend. Default returns "create table <name> (".
requirements: tableName should be a valid identifier for the backend.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::drop_table
functions.description: Returns a DROP TABLE statement for the given table. Default returns "drop table <name>".
requirements: tableName should be a valid identifier.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::truncate_table
functions.description: Returns a TRUNCATE TABLE statement for the given table. Default returns "truncate table <name>".
requirements: tableName should be a valid identifier.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::create_column_type
functions.signature: virtual std::string soci::details::session_backend::create_column_type(soci::db_type dt, int precision, int scale)
functions.description: Returns the backend-specific SQL type for a given db_type and optional precision/scale to be used in DDL. Default models PostgreSQL types.
requirements: dt must be a supported soci::db_type; otherwise default throws soci_error in some cases (e.g., unsupported types).
precision/scale semantics depend on dt; precision==0 often selects unbounded type.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::create_column_type
functions.signature: std::string soci::details::session_backend::create_column_type(soci::data_type dt, int precision, int scale)
functions.description: Deprecated overload that maps legacy data_type to db_type and forwards to create_column_type(db_type,...).
requirements: dt must be a valid soci::data_type.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::add_column
functions.signature: virtual std::string soci::details::session_backend::add_column(const std::string& tableName, const std::string& columnName, soci::db_type dt, int precision, int scale)
functions.description: Returns an ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN statement for the given name/type using create_column_type().
requirements: tableName and columnName must be valid identifiers.
dt, precision, scale must be valid for create_column_type().

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::add_column
functions.signature: std::string soci::details::session_backend::add_column(const std::string& tableName, const std::string& columnName, soci::data_type dt, int precision, int scale)
functions.description: Deprecated overload that maps legacy data_type to db_type and returns an ADD COLUMN statement.
requirements: tableName and columnName must be valid identifiers.
dt must be a valid soci::data_type.

functions.name: soci::details::session_backend::alter_column
functions.signature: virtual std::string soci::details::session_backend::alter_column(const std::string& tableName, const std::string& columnName, soci::db_type dt, int precision, int scale)
functions.description: Returns an ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN TYPE statement using create_column_type().
requirements: tableName and columnName must be valid identifiers.
dt, precision, scale must be valid for create_column_type().

functions.name: soci::fopen
functions.signature: FILE* soci::fopen(const char* filename, const char* mode)
functions.description: Opens a C FILE stream for the given filename using the specified mode. On MSVC builds this is a thin wrapper around fopen_s; on other platforms it aliases std::fopen. Returns a FILE* on success or nullptr on failure. Use std::fclose() to close the returned stream.
requirements: filename must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
mode must be a valid, null-terminated C string accepted by the C runtime (e.g., "r", "w", "rb", etc.).
On success, the returned FILE* must be closed with std::fclose to avoid resource leaks.
Caller must check for nullptr to detect errors (e.g., file not found, permission denied).
On MSVC, invalid parameters may trigger the runtime-constraint handler in the underlying fopen_s; do not pass null pointers.

functions.name: soci::getenv
functions.description: Retrieves the value of the environment variable with the given name. On MSVC builds this wrapper calls std::getenv and returns the resulting pointer as const char*. Returns nullptr if the variable is not found. The returned pointer refers to internal storage that may change on subsequent environment queries.
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string naming an environment variable.
The returned pointer may be nullptr if the variable is not set; callers must check for nullptr before use.
The returned buffer must be treated as read-only and may be invalidated by subsequent calls to getenv/putenv/setenv or by environment changes; copy it if persistence is needed.
Not thread-safe across concurrent modifications of the environment.

functions.name: soci::sscanf
functions.signature: int soci::sscanf(const char* str, const char* format, ...)
functions.description: Parses input from the string str according to format and stores the results into the additional pointer arguments. On MSVC builds this wrapper forwards to vsscanf_s (secure variant), which enforces additional size-argument requirements for certain specifiers; on other platforms it aliases std::sscanf. Returns the number of input items successfully matched and assigned, or EOF on failure before any assignment.
requirements: str must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
format must be a valid, null-terminated C format string matching the provided arguments.
All additional arguments must be valid pointers to storage appropriate for their corresponding format specifiers.
On MSVC (vsscanf_s): for %s, %c, and %[ specifiers, you must provide an additional size argument indicating the destination buffer size in characters; otherwise the call fails.
Caller must check the return value to determine how many items were assigned and handle partial matches or errors.

functions.name: soci::strncpy
functions.signature: char* soci::strncpy(char* dest, const char* src, size_t n)
functions.description: Copies characters from src to dest with an upper bound. On MSVC builds this wrapper calls strncpy_s(dest, n, src, _TRUNCATE) and always null-terminates if n > 0, truncating as needed; on other platforms it aliases std::strncpy, which copies up to n characters and may not null-terminate if src is longer than or equal to n. Returns dest.
requirements: dest must point to a valid writable buffer.
src must be a valid, null-terminated C string.
n must be the size in bytes of the destination buffer.
On MSVC (strncpy_s with _TRUNCATE): passing null pointers or an incorrect n may trigger a runtime-constraint violation; when n > 0, the destination will be null-terminated, and truncation can occur.
On non-MSVC (std::strncpy): if src length >= n, the result is not guaranteed to be null-terminated; callers should ensure space for the terminator or add it manually.
dest must have capacity of at least n bytes to avoid buffer overflow.

functions.name: soci_create_session
functions.description: Creates and returns an opaque database session handle using the provided connection string. Use this to open a SOCI C API session before creating statements or blobs.
requirements: connectionString must point to a valid, null-terminated string
The returned session_handle must be destroyed with soci_destroy_session when no longer needed
Do not pass the returned handle to other functions until soci_create_session succeeds

functions.name: soci_destroy_session

requirements: s must be a valid session_handle obtained from soci_create_session

It is safe to call only once per created session (no double-destroy)

functions.name: soci_begin

functions.name: soci_commit

functions.name: soci_rollback

functions.name: soci::type_conversion<std::optional<T>>::from_base
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
static void soci::type_conversion<std::optional<T>>::from_base(
    typename soci::type_conversion<T>::base_type const & in,
    soci::indicator ind,
    std::optional<T> & out)
functions.description: Converts a database/base value and its indicator into a std::optional<T>. If ind == soci::i_null, the output optional is reset to empty. Otherwise, it creates a temporary T and delegates conversion to soci::type_conversion<T>::from_base, then assigns the resulting value to the optional. Intended for SOCI’s automatic type conversion for std::optional values.
requirements: A valid soci::type_conversion<T> specialization must exist, defining base_type and providing from_base/to_base for T.
The input indicator must correctly describe the nullness of the base value; if ind == soci::i_null, 'in' is treated as NULL and 'out' becomes disengaged.
When ind != soci::i_null, 'in' must be a valid value of typename soci::type_conversion<T>::base_type suitable for soci::type_conversion<T>::from_base.
The 'out' parameter must be a valid reference to a std::optional<T> that can be modified.
Any exceptions or errors from soci::type_conversion<T>::from_base may propagate; callers should be prepared to handle them.

functions.signature:

static void soci::type_conversion<std::optional<T>>::to_base(
    std::optional<T> const & in,
    typename soci::type_conversion<T>::base_type & out,
    soci::indicator & ind)
functions.description: Converts a std::optional<T> into a database/base value and indicator. If the optional contains a value, delegates to soci::type_conversion<T>::to_base(*in, out, ind). If the optional is empty, sets ind = soci::i_null to represent a NULL value; 'out' is left unchanged by this function in that case.
requirements: A valid soci::type_conversion<T> specialization must exist, defining base_type and providing to_base for T.
If 'in' contains a value, '*in' must be a valid T for conversion by soci::type_conversion<T>::to_base.
The 'out' parameter must be a valid reference to a base value object of type typename soci::type_conversion<T>::base_type to receive the converted value.
The 'ind' parameter is an output parameter; the function will set it to soci::i_null when 'in' is empty and otherwise relies on soci::type_conversion<T>::to_base to set it appropriately.
Any exceptions or errors from soci::type_conversion<T>::to_base may propagate; callers should be prepared to handle them.

functions.name: soci::transaction::transaction
functions.description: Constructor for a scoped/RAII database transaction bound to the given soci::session. In typical SOCI usage, constructing this object begins a database transaction on the provided session and tracks whether it has been explicitly handled (committed or rolled back). Usual pattern: create a transaction, execute statements, then call commit(); if not committed, the destructor will typically roll back. Note: The header does not show side effects; behavior is inferred from SOCI transaction conventions.
requirements: sql must be a valid soci::session object that remains alive for the entire lifetime of the transaction object (lifetime requirement inferred from the reference parameter).

The session should be in a state that allows starting a transaction (e.g., connected and not already within an incompatible transaction context) — inferred from naming and common transaction semantics.
Do not destroy or move the referenced session while the transaction exists.

functions.name: soci::transaction::~transaction
functions.description: Destructor for the transaction object. In common SOCI patterns, if the transaction has not been explicitly committed or rolled back, the destructor will roll back to ensure strong exception safety. Exact side effects are not shown in this header and are inferred from the class purpose and naming.
requirements: Must not be invoked after the associated soci::session has been destroyed (the transaction object must be destroyed first).
Callers should ensure any necessary commit() or rollback() is performed before destruction if they rely on a specific outcome; otherwise, typical behavior is to roll back on destruction (inferred).

functions.name: soci::transaction::commit
functions.description: Explicitly commit the active transaction associated with this object’s session. After a successful commit, the transaction is considered handled and typically won’t be rolled back in the destructor. Behavior details (exceptions, return codes) are not specified here and are inferred from SOCI conventions.
requirements: Must be called only when a transaction is active and not yet handled (i.e., before any prior commit() or rollback()) — inferred from transaction semantics.
The underlying soci::session must still be valid and open.
Do not call both commit() and rollback() on the same transaction instance (call at most one) — inferred.

functions.name: soci::transaction::rollback
functions.description: Explicitly roll back the active transaction associated with this object’s session. After a successful rollback, the transaction is considered handled and typically won’t perform any action in the destructor. Exact error/exception behavior is not specified here and is inferred from SOCI conventions.
requirements: Must be called only when a transaction is active and not yet handled (i.e., before any prior commit() or rollback()) — inferred from transaction semantics.
The underlying soci::session must still be valid and open.
Do not call both rollback() and commit() on the same transaction instance (call at most one) — inferred.

functions.name: soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::trivial_blob_backend
functions.description: Constructs a trivial_blob_backend bound to the provided session backend. This implementation keeps BLOB data in an internal memory buffer and interacts with the database session backend only via the base backend interface.
requirements: backend must refer to a valid soci::details::session_backend object that outlives the trivial_blob_backend instance (lifetime requirement inferred from the stored reference).
No exceptions are thrown by the constructor under normal circumstances (no explicit throws).

functions.name: soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::get_len
functions.description: Returns the current length, in bytes, of the internal BLOB buffer.
requirements: May be called at any time after construction.
No arguments and no preconditions.

functions.name: soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::read_from_start
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::read_from_start(void* buf, std::size_t toRead, std::size_t offset = 0)
functions.description: Reads up to toRead bytes from the internal buffer starting at byte offset into the caller-provided memory at buf. The function clamps the read size to the available data and returns the number of bytes actually read. Throws soci_error if the read would start past the end of the BLOB.
requirements: offset must be strictly less than the current length returned by get_len(), unless the BLOB is empty (length 0), in which case offset may be 0; otherwise a soci_error is thrown.
buf must point to writable memory of at least the number of bytes returned; if toRead > 0, buf must be non-null (memcpy is used).
toRead may be any size; the function will reduce it to fit within the available data from offset.
Callers should be prepared to handle soci_error exceptions for invalid offsets.

functions.name: soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::write_from_start
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::write_from_start(const void* buf, std::size_t toWrite, std::size_t offset = 0)
functions.description: Writes toWrite bytes from buf into the internal buffer starting at byte offset. The buffer is resized as needed to accommodate the write. Returns the number of bytes written (equal to toWrite). Throws soci_error if offset is greater than the current length.
requirements: offset must be less than or equal to the current length returned by get_len(); if offset > length, a soci_error is thrown.
buf must point to readable memory of at least toWrite bytes; if toWrite > 0, buf must be non-null (memcpy is used).
The write may reallocate the internal buffer; any previously obtained pointer from get_buffer() may be invalidated.
Callers should be prepared to handle soci_error exceptions for invalid offsets.

functions.name: soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::append
functions.description: Appends toWrite bytes from buf to the end of the internal buffer. Returns the number of bytes appended (equal to toWrite).
requirements: buf must point to readable memory of at least toWrite bytes; if toWrite > 0, buf must be non-null.
The operation may reallocate the internal buffer; any previously obtained pointer from get_buffer() may be invalidated.

functions.name: soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::trim
functions.description: Resizes the internal buffer to newLen bytes. If newLen is smaller than the current size, the data is truncated. If larger, the buffer grows and the new bytes are value-initialized (zero for uint8_t).
requirements: newLen may be any non-negative size representable by std::size_t.
Resizing may reallocate the internal buffer; any previously obtained pointer from get_buffer() may be invalidated.

functions.name: soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::set_data
functions.description: Replaces the current contents of the internal buffer with toWrite bytes copied from buf, returning the number of bytes written. Equivalent to clearing the buffer and then writing from offset 0.
requirements: buf must point to readable memory of at least toWrite bytes; if toWrite > 0, buf must be non-null.
Operation may reallocate the internal buffer; any previously obtained pointer from get_buffer() may be invalidated.

functions.name: soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::get_buffer
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal contiguous storage of the BLOB data. Intended for read-only access to the current buffer content.
requirements: The returned pointer is valid for get_len() bytes at the time of the call; it may be invalidated by any subsequent non-const operation on the object (e.g., write, append, trim, set_data).
If get_len() is 0, the returned pointer must not be dereferenced.
The caller must not write through the returned pointer.

functions.name: soci::details::trivial_blob_backend::get_session_backend
functions.description: Returns a reference to the associated session backend object used by this BLOB backend.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the trivial_blob_backend object exists and the referenced session_backend outlives it.

functions.name: soci::type_conversion<T,Enable>::from_base
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Enable>
static void soci::type_conversion<T, Enable>::from_base(base_type const& in, indicator ind, T& out)
functions.description: Converts a database base_type value to the user type T by copy. Intended as the default pass-through for SOCI when no custom conversion is needed. If ind indicates a NULL value, the function throws soci_error. Copies ‘in’ to ‘out’.
requirements: ind must not be i_null; otherwise soci_error("Null value not allowed for this type") is thrown at runtime.
T must be constructible from base_type const& (enforced by static_assert).
out must be a valid lvalue reference to T.

functions.name: soci::type_conversion<T,Enable>::move_from_base
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Enable>
static void soci::type_conversion<T, Enable>::move_from_base(base_type& in, indicator ind, T& out)
functions.description: Moves a database base_type value into the user type T. Intended for optimized move-based conversion. If ind indicates a NULL value, throws soci_error. Moves ‘in’ into ‘out’, potentially leaving ‘in’ in a moved-from state.
requirements: ind must not be i_null; otherwise soci_error("Null value not allowed for this type") is thrown at runtime.
base_type must not be const and T must be constructible from base_type&& (enforced by static_assert).
out must be a valid lvalue reference to T.
Caller should not rely on the state of ‘in’ after the call (moved-from state).

functions.name: soci::type_conversion<T,Enable>::to_base
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Enable>
static void soci::type_conversion<T, Enable>::to_base(T const& in, base_type& out, indicator& ind)
functions.description: Converts a user type T to the database base_type by copy and marks the indicator as not-null. Assigns ‘in’ to ‘out’ and sets ind = i_ok.
requirements: out must be a valid lvalue reference to base_type.
ind must be a valid lvalue reference; it will be set to i_ok.

functions.name: soci::type_conversion<T,Enable>::move_to_base
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename Enable>
static void soci::type_conversion<T, Enable>::move_to_base(T& in, base_type& out, indicator& ind)
functions.description: Moves a user type T into the database base_type and marks the indicator as not-null. Moves ‘in’ into ‘out’ and sets ind = i_ok. ‘in’ may be left in a moved-from state.
requirements: out must be a valid lvalue reference to base_type.
ind must be a valid lvalue reference; it will be set to i_ok.
Caller should not rely on the state of ‘in’ after the call (moved-from state).

functions.name: soci::details::can_use_from_base
functions.signature:
template <typename Trait>
constexpr typename std::enable_if<soci::details::supports_from_base_check<Trait>::value, bool>::type
soci::details::can_use_from_base()
functions.description: Compile-time utility that returns whether a conversion trait’s from_base should be usable, based on the presence and value of Trait::from_base_check. This overload participates only if Trait defines from_base_check.
requirements: Trait must define a nested from_base_check with a constexpr bool value member (i.e., Trait::from_base_check::value) for this overload to participate.
No runtime requirements; evaluated at compile time.

functions.name: soci::details::can_use_move_from_base
functions.signature:
template <typename Trait>
constexpr typename std::enable_if<soci::details::supports_move_from_base_check<Trait>::value, bool>::type
soci::details::can_use_move_from_base()
functions.description: Compile-time utility that returns whether a conversion trait’s move_from_base should be usable, based on the presence and value of Trait::move_from_base_check. This overload participates only if Trait defines move_from_base_check.
requirements: Trait must define a nested move_from_base_check with a constexpr bool value member (i.e., Trait::move_from_base_check::value) for this overload to participate.
No runtime requirements; evaluated at compile time.

functions.name: soci::details::do_into
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::into_type_ptr soci::details::do_into(T & t, soci::details::user_type_tag)
functions.description: Factory for creating an into binding for a user-defined type T using SOCI's type_conversion<T>. Returns a heap-allocated conversion_into_type<T> wrapped in into_type_ptr, which the SOCI core uses to receive data from the database into t.
requirements: T must have a valid soci::type_conversion<T> specialization providing base_type and from_base/to_base conversions.
t must remain alive at least until the associated statement/fetch cycle using the returned into binding completes.
user_type_tag is a dispatch tag used internally by SOCI; pass an instance of soci::details::user_type_tag when calling directly.

functions.name: soci::details::do_use
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::use_type_ptr soci::details::do_use(T & t, std::string const & name, soci::details::user_type_tag)
functions.description: Factory for creating a use binding (input parameter) for a user-defined type T using type_conversion<T>. Binds t to a statement parameter identified optionally by name.
requirements: T must have a valid soci::type_conversion<T> specialization.
t must remain alive until the statement execution(s) using this binding completes.
name, if non-empty, must match the parameter name expected by the SQL statement or backend.

functions.name: soci::details::checked_ptr_cast
functions.signature:
template <typename T, typename U>
T* soci::details::checked_ptr_cast(U* ptr)
functions.description: Safely check at runtime whether ptr points to an object whose type matches T and, if so, return it as T*. This is a lightweight alternative to dynamic_cast when only exact type equality is needed. It compares RTTI type_info of the pointed-to object with typeid(T) and returns NULL if they differ; otherwise it performs a static_cast to T*. Note: the input pointer must be non-null because the function dereferences it to obtain type information.
requirements: ptr must be non-null (the function evaluates typeid(*ptr)).
T* must be a valid static_cast target from U* at compile time (otherwise the template instantiation will fail to compile).
RTTI must be enabled; typeid must reflect the runtime type of *ptr for the check to be meaningful (polymorphic types recommended).
If the dynamic type of *ptr is not exactly T, the function returns NULL; it does not throw.

functions.name: soci::details::holder::make_holder
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
static soci::details::holder* soci::details::holder::make_holder(T* val)
functions.description: Factory method that creates a new holder owning the given pointer to a value of type T. The holder records the corresponding db_type via type_holder_trait<T> and will delete the stored pointer in its destructor. Use this to wrap a dynamically allocated value for type-erased storage and later retrieval via holder::get.
requirements: T must have a valid specialization of soci::details::type_holder_trait<T> mapping it to a db_type (e.g., std::string, std::wstring, (u)int{8,16,32,64}_t, double, std::tm, soci::blob, and library-specific integer aliases).
val should point to a dynamically allocated object obtained with operator new; the holder assumes ownership and will delete it with delete.
The dynamic type of *val must match T exactly and be consistent with the selected db_type to avoid undefined behavior in the destructor and get().
Passing nullptr is technically permitted (delete on nullptr is a no-op) but subsequent get() calls will dereference it and likely throw or crash; callers should provide a valid, initialized object.

functions.name: soci::details::holder::~holder
functions.description: Destructor that releases the owned value stored in the holder by deleting the pointer according to the recorded db_type. It prevents leaks for values created via make_holder or otherwise passed to the holder constructor. After destruction, the holder and its contained pointer must not be used.
requirements: The stored pointer must have been allocated with operator new and must not be deleted elsewhere (holder has unique ownership).
The recorded db_type must correspond to the actual pointed-to type (mismatches yield undefined behavior).
Do not access the holder or the stored value after the holder is destroyed.

functions.name: soci::details::holder::get
functions.description: Return the stored value converted to T by value. Performs type-safe conversions using soci_cast: identical types return directly; supported integral widenings are bounds-checked; double, std::tm, strings, wstrings are converted only when T exactly matches; blobs can be converted into contiguous, resizable byte containers (e.g., std::string, std::vector<char>) by copying blob content. Throws std::bad_cast on incompatible conversions.
requirements: The holder must currently contain a value compatible with the requested T; otherwise the function throws std::bad_cast.
For integral conversions, only widening (or range-compatible) conversions are allowed; out-of-range values cause std::bad_cast.
Converting a blob requires T to satisfy is_contiguous_resizable_container_v<T> (e.g., std::string; std::vector<T> where sizeof(T)==1) so that data() and resize() semantics are valid.
When converting a blob to a container, T’s element size must be 1 byte; the container will be resized to the blob size and filled via copy.
If the stored pointer is null, any attempt to access it during conversion results in undefined behavior; callers should ensure the holder was created with a valid object.

functions.name: soci::details::type_ptr::type_ptr
functions.description: Constructor that takes ownership of a raw pointer to T. On destruction of the type_ptr instance, the managed pointer will be deleted unless released beforehand. Typical usage: allocate with new, pass the pointer to the constructor, and use get() to access it. Use release() if you need to relinquish ownership without deleting the object.
requirements: Argument p may be null or a valid pointer to a T allocated with operator new (delete-compatible).
After construction, the type_ptr instance owns p and will delete it in the destructor unless release() is called.
Do not pass a pointer that must be freed by a mechanism other than delete (e.g., malloc/free or custom deleter).
Do not use the managed object through other owners that will also delete it (avoid double-ownership).

functions.name: soci::details::type_ptr::~type_ptr
functions.description: Destructor that deletes the managed pointer using delete. If release() was called earlier, the stored pointer will be null and nothing will be deleted.
requirements: The managed pointer must either be null or point to a T allocated with operator new that can be safely deleted.
Callers must not use the managed object after the type_ptr is destroyed unless ownership was explicitly taken via get() + release().

functions.name: soci::details::type_ptr::get
functions.description: Returns the raw managed pointer without transferring ownership. The returned pointer may be null. Intended for read or non-owning access to the managed object.
requirements: The returned pointer must not be deleted by the caller unless ownership has been taken by subsequently calling release().
The returned pointer may be null; callers must check for null before dereferencing.
The pointer becomes invalid when the type_ptr is destroyed (unless ownership has been taken via release()).

functions.name: soci::details::type_ptr::release
functions.description: Relinquishes ownership by setting the internal pointer to null without deleting the managed object. This does not return the pointer; callers should first capture it via get(), then call release() to prevent deletion at destruction.
requirements: If the caller intends to assume ownership, it must call get() to obtain the current pointer before calling release(), as release() does not return the pointer.
After release(), the type_ptr will no longer delete the object; the caller becomes responsible for deleting it exactly once via delete.
May be called multiple times; subsequent calls have no effect once the internal pointer is null.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_base::~use_type_base
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the base class of all input-binding helpers. Ensures proper cleanup via base pointer.
requirements: May be invoked polymorphically; derived classes must provide proper cleanup in their overrides of clean_up().
Object should be destroyed only after any associated statement/Backend resources have been released or after clean_up() has been called by the framework.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_base::bind
functions.description: Pure virtual. Binds the wrapped data to a statement at the given parameter position. Typically advances the position for subsequent bindings.
requirements: st must reference a valid, prepared soci::details::statement_impl.
position must reference a valid parameter index within the statement’s bind range; on success, implementations usually advance it to the next position.
Caller must respect the statement’s binding order and lifecycle (bind before execution).

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_base::get_name
functions.description: Pure virtual. Returns the named parameter identifier, if any, for this binding (e.g., ":name"). Empty string if unnamed.
requirements: May be called after construction; must not throw except as documented by implementations.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_base::dump_value
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::use_type_base::dump_value(std::ostream& os, int index) const = 0;
functions.description: Pure virtual. Writes a textual representation of the bound value at the given element index to the provided stream. Used for diagnostics/logging.
requirements: os must be a valid std::ostream reference.
index must be within the valid element range [0, size()).

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_base::pre_exec
functions.description: Pure virtual lifecycle hook invoked before statement execution. Allows implementors to prepare buffers for executing num elements (e.g., array binding).
requirements: num is the number of elements to execute; must be non-negative.
Typically called by the SOCI framework; callers outside the framework should not invoke it directly.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_base::pre_use
functions.description: Pure virtual lifecycle hook invoked before binding/use. Implementations may convert or stage user data to backend format.
requirements: Called by the SOCI framework prior to binding/execution; external callers should not invoke it directly.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_base::post_use
functions.description: Pure virtual lifecycle hook invoked after use/execution. Allows implementors to propagate data back to user objects (e.g., OUT parameters).
requirements: gotData indicates whether backend returned data to propagate.
Called by the SOCI framework; external callers should not invoke it directly.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_base::clean_up
functions.description: Pure virtual. Releases any backend resources allocated by bind or pre_exec.
requirements: Called by the SOCI framework when the binding is no longer needed.
Implementations must be idempotent or safely handle multiple invocations during teardown.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type_base::size
functions.description: Pure virtual. Returns the number of elements represented by this binding (1 for scalars, N for vectors/arrays).
requirements: Must be callable at any time after construction.
Return value must accurately reflect the bound range.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type::standard_use_type
functions.signature: soci::details::standard_use_type::standard_use_type(void* data, soci::exchange_type type, bool readOnly, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a scalar binding for a single value. data points to the user object; type identifies the SOCI exchange type; readOnly denotes const/IN binding; name is the optional named parameter.
requirements: data must be a non-null pointer to an object whose C++ type matches type (as per SOCI exchange_traits).
If readOnly is true, data should point to a const object and will not be modified by the backend.
name may be empty or a driver-appropriate parameter name string.
The pointed-to object must outlive this standard_use_type instance and any statement execution using it.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type::standard_use_type
functions.signature: soci::details::standard_use_type::standard_use_type(void* data, soci::exchange_type type, soci::indicator& ind, bool readOnly, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a scalar binding with an associated indicator (NULL/defined state). data points to the user object; type identifies the exchange type; ind tracks nullability; readOnly denotes const/IN binding; name is optional.
requirements: data must be a non-null pointer to an object compatible with type.
&ind must remain valid for the binding’s lifetime and during execution.
If readOnly is true, data should point to a const object; the backend will not modify it.
The pointed-to object and ind must outlive this binding and any statement execution using it.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type::~standard_use_type
functions.description: Destructor. Releases any backend-specific resources acquired during binding for scalar values.
requirements: Should be called only after clean_up() has been performed by the framework or when no backend resources remain in use.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type::bind
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::standard_use_type::bind(soci::details::statement_impl& st, int& position) override;
functions.description: Binds the scalar data (and optional indicator) to the given statement at the specified parameter position. Typically advances position.
requirements: st must reference a valid, prepared soci::details::statement_impl.
position must reference a valid parameter index; on success, it is typically incremented by 1.
Must be called before statement execution.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type::get_name
functions.description: Returns the named parameter identifier provided at construction time, or an empty string if unnamed.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type::dump_value
functions.signature: virtual void soci::details::standard_use_type::dump_value(std::ostream& os, int index) const override;
functions.description: Writes a textual representation of the scalar value to os. index must be 0 for scalar bindings.
requirements: os must be valid.
index must be 0 for scalar bindings.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type::get_data
functions.description: Returns the raw pointer to the bound scalar data. Useful for custom backends or conversions.
requirements: Returned pointer is the same as provided at construction and must be interpreted according to the exchange type.
Caller must ensure proper type casting and const-correctness.

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type::convert_to_base
functions.description: Conversion hook executed before binding to convert a user-defined type to a SOCI base type. Default implementation does nothing.
requirements: If overridden, must leave data_ consistent with type and ready for binding.
Should be invoked by the framework during pre_use().

functions.name: soci::details::standard_use_type::convert_from_base
functions.description: Conversion hook executed after use/execution to convert from a SOCI base type back to the user-defined type. Default implementation does nothing.
requirements: If overridden, must read from the bound base value and update the user object safely.
Should be invoked by the framework during post_use().

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type::vector_use_type
functions.signature: soci::details::vector_use_type::vector_use_type(void* data, soci::exchange_type type, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a vector/array binding without indicators, covering the entire vector. data points to a std::vector<T>; type is the element exchange type; name is optional.
requirements: data must be a non-null pointer to a std::vector<T> whose element type corresponds to type (per SOCI exchange_traits).
The pointed-to vector must outlive this binding and any statement executions.
name may be empty or a driver-appropriate parameter name.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type::vector_use_type
functions.signature: soci::details::vector_use_type::vector_use_type(void* data, soci::exchange_type type, std::size_t begin, std::size_t* end, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a vector/array binding over a subrange [begin, *end) if end is non-null, otherwise from begin to the container’s current end. No indicators.
requirements: data must point to a std::vector<T> compatible with type.
If end is non-null, *end must be <= the vector’s size and >= begin.
begin must be <= the vector’s size.
The vector and the object pointed to by end (if provided) must outlive the binding and execution.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type::vector_use_type
functions.signature: soci::details::vector_use_type::vector_use_type(void* data, soci::exchange_type type, std::vector<soci::indicator> const& ind, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a vector/array binding with an indicators vector covering the entire container.
requirements: data must point to a std::vector<T> compatible with type.
&ind must remain valid while the binding is in use; its size should be at least the number of elements bound.
The vector must outlive the binding and execution.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type::vector_use_type
functions.signature: soci::details::vector_use_type::vector_use_type(void* data, soci::exchange_type type, std::vector<soci::indicator> const& ind, std::size_t begin, std::size_t* end, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a vector/array binding over a subrange with an indicators vector.
requirements: data must point to a std::vector<T> compatible with type.
If end is non-null, *end must be <= the vector’s size and >= begin; begin must be <= vector size.
&ind must remain valid for the binding’s lifetime and provide indicators for the bound range (size sufficient for [begin, effective_end)).
The vector and the object pointed to by end (if provided) must outlive the binding and execution.

functions.name: soci::details::vector_use_type::~vector_use_type
functions.description: Destructor. Releases any backend-specific resources acquired during vector/array binding.
requirements: Should be called only after clean_up() has been performed by the framework or when no backend resources remain in use.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<T>::use_type
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::use_type<T>::use_type(T& t, std::string const& name = std::string());

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<T>::use_type
functions.signature:

soci::details::use_type<T>::use_type(T const& t, std::string const& name = std::string());

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<T>::use_type
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::use_type<T>::use_type(T& t, soci::indicator& ind, std::string const& name = std::string());

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<T>::use_type
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::use_type<T>::use_type(T const& t, soci::indicator& ind, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a read-only scalar binding for const T with an associated indicator reference.
requirements: t and ind must remain alive during binding and statement execution.
Binding is read-only; backend will not modify t.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<std::vector<T> >::use_type
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::use_type<std::vector<T> >::use_type(std::vector<T>& v, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a vector binding over the entire vector v without indicators.
requirements: v must outlive the binding and execution.
name is optional.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<std::vector<T> >::use_type
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::use_type<std::vector<T> >::use_type(std::vector<T>& v, std::size_t begin, std::size_t* end, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a vector binding over the subrange [begin, *end) if end is provided; otherwise [begin, v.size()).
requirements: v must outlive the binding and execution.
If end is non-null, *end must be <= v.size() and >= begin; begin must be <= v.size().

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<std::vector<T> >::use_type
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
soci::details::use_type<std::vector<T> >::use_type(std::vector<T> const& v, std::string const& name = std::string());
functions.description: Constructs a read-only vector binding over the entire const vector v without indicators.
requirements: v must outlive the binding and execution.
Binding is read-only; backend will not modify v.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<std::vector<T> >::use_type

functions.name: soci::details::use_container<T, soci::details::no_indicator>::use_container
functions.description: Constructor for the specialization soci::details::use_container<T, no_indicator>. It initializes a wrapper that holds references to a user variable (t) and an optional parameter name (name) for binding values without an indicator in SOCI. Typically created via soci::use(var[, name]) overloads when no indicator is provided. Notes: stores references, not copies; intended to be a lightweight binder for subsequent database statement preparation/execution. Some details are inferred from naming and structure; the header provides no additional runtime behavior documentation.
requirements: Parameter _t must be an lvalue (non-temporary) because it is stored as T&.
The object referenced by _t must outlive the use_container instance and any operation that uses it (e.g., statement execution) since only a reference is stored.

Parameter _name is stored as const std::string&; the referenced string must outlive the use_container instance. Avoid passing a temporary for name unless its lifetime is guaranteed to cover all uses of the container.
Construction does not copy _t or _name; both are retained by reference.
Assignment of use_container is disabled (SOCI_NOT_ASSIGNABLE); do not rely on assignment semantics.

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<values>::bind
functions.description: Binds the soci::values instance to a statement for execution. It syncs the values’ column-name case with the session, converts the user representation to the base representation (via convert_to_base), and calls st.bind(v_). Typically invoked by the SOCI framework during statement preparation/execution, not directly by user code.
requirements: st must reference a valid soci::details::statement_impl associated with a live session (st.session_)
The referenced soci::values (internal v_) must be valid and remain alive for the duration of the bind and subsequent execution
The position argument is ignored by this implementation
If convert_to_base() is overridden in a derived class, it must leave v_ in a state acceptable to st.bind(v_)

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<values>::get_name
functions.description: Builds and returns a comma-separated, parenthesized list of column names from the bound values object, e.g., "(col1, col2)". Used by SOCI to generate parameter/column lists for SQL diagnostics or metadata.
requirements: The underlying soci::values must have its columns/properties defined; otherwise the result may be an empty list "()"
The function does not modify state

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<values>::dump_value
functions.description: Writes a placeholder textual representation of the bound value(s) to the given stream. Current implementation outputs the literal "<value>" regardless of index. Intended primarily for debugging/logging hooks.
requirements: os must be a valid output stream ready for writing
index is ignored by this implementation

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<values>::pre_exec
functions.description: Pre-execution hook for use bindings. This implementation is a no-op. Called by SOCI before executing a statement, potentially with the number of executions for bulk operations.
requirements: No specific requirements; num is ignored by this implementation

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<values>::post_use
functions.description: Post-use hook invoked after statement execution. Resets the values’ internal get counter and converts from base representation back to the user representation via convert_from_base().
requirements: The underlying soci::values must be valid and bound for the duration of the call
gotData is ignored by this implementation
If convert_from_base() is overridden, it must correctly interpret v_'s base representation produced by execution/binding

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<values>::pre_use
functions.description: Pre-use hook invoked before statement execution. Converts the user representation to the base representation via convert_to_base().
requirements: The underlying soci::values must be valid for the duration of the call

requirements: The underlying soci::values must be valid at the time of the call

functions.name: soci::details::use_type<values>::size

requirements: None; the function is const and has no side effects

functions.description: Virtual hook for converting from a user-defined representation to the base representation stored/bound in soci::values before execution. The base class implementation is a no-op; derived classes may override to implement custom conversions.

requirements: If overridden in a derived class, it must correctly handle whatever base data was produced and must not invalidate v_
