functions.name: soci::values::values
functions.description: Default constructor for soci::values. Initializes an empty values container with no associated row, the internal get counter set to 0, and column-name uppercasing disabled. Intended to be used as a holder for named/positional values (e.g., for use/bind operations) or as a target for into conversions.
requirements: No arguments required.
Object starts detached from any row; methods that rely on an attached row will behave accordingly (e.g., get_number_of_columns returns 0).

functions.name: soci::values::get_indicator
functions.description: Returns the indicator (e.g., i_ok, i_null) for the column at the given 0-based position. When a row is attached, it queries the row; otherwise it uses locally stored indicators for values set via set().
requirements: pos must refer to a valid column/index present in the underlying row or in the locally stored values; otherwise behavior is unspecified and may throw at definition time (not visible in this header).
May throw soci_error or other exceptions depending on the underlying implementation if pos is out of range or no indicator is available.

functions.name: soci::values::get_indicator
functions.description: Returns the indicator for the column/value identified by name. When a row is attached, it queries by column name; otherwise it uses locally stored values previously set with set(name, ...).
requirements: name must correspond to an existing column in the attached row or a value previously set via set(name, ...); otherwise the underlying implementation may throw an exception.
Name matching may be affected by uppercase_column_names settings at the row level; this function itself just forwards the request.

functions.name: soci::values::skip
functions.description: Advances the current extraction position by num columns/fields. If a row is attached, forwards to row_->skip(num); otherwise advances the internal position counter used by operator>>.
requirements: num must be non-negative (std::size_t).
If a row is attached, any requirements of row::skip(num) apply (e.g., not skipping past the end).
When no row is attached, caller should ensure not to advance past the number of locally stored values to avoid subsequent out-of-range access when extracting.

functions.name: soci::values::reset_get_counter
functions.description: Resets the internal extraction position counter to the beginning. If a row is attached, forwards to row_->reset_get_counter(); otherwise sets the local counter to 0.
requirements: If a row is attached, any preconditions of row::reset_get_counter() apply (unspecified here).
Safe to call at any time to restart sequential extraction.

functions.description: Sets or updates a named value with the given name and value, storing an associated indicator. Converts value to the backend base type using type_conversion<T>::to_base and keeps an internal deep copy for later binding/extraction.
requirements: type_conversion<T> must be defined and provide base_type, to_base, and from_base semantics compatible with SOCI.
name must be a non-empty string; if not previously present, it is inserted and indexed; if already present, its stored indicator and value are updated.
indic should be a valid SOCI indicator (e.g., i_ok, i_null).
If indic is i_ok, type_conversion<T>::to_base must succeed; exceptions from conversion will propagate.
Memory management: the function allocates internal storage for the value and indicator; these are cleaned up by values::clean_up() or statement cleanup paths.

indic should be a valid SOCI indicator (e.g., i_ok, i_null).

functions.description: Associates an output (into) variable with the statement by positional index for the empty backend. Intended to map application storage (pointed to by data) to a column result at the given position according to the SOCI exchange_type. Function must be called during statement setup/binding phase before execution.

functions.description: Prepares the bound standard into value before fetching rows. Typically used by backends to reset buffers or state. Behavior specifics for the empty backend are not documented.

functions.name: soci::empty_standard_into_type_backend::post_fetch
functions.description: Finalizes the transfer of a fetched value into the user buffer after a fetch operation. gotData indicates whether a row was obtained; ind allows setting null/defined state. Empty-backend specifics are not documented.
requirements: If ind is non-null, it must point to valid indicator storage for the corresponding bound value.
Must be called after pre_fetch/fetch cycle.
gotData indicates whether data were produced for the bound position; callers should pass the correct flag from execute/fetch results.

functions.name: soci::empty_standard_into_type_backend::clean_up
functions.description: Releases any resources associated with the standard into binding for the empty backend. Typically invoked when the statement is destroyed or re-bound.
requirements: May only be called after a previous define_by_pos on the same instance.

functions.name: soci::empty_vector_into_type_backend::define_by_pos
functions.signature: void soci::empty_vector_into_type_backend::define_by_pos(int& position, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type)
functions.description: Associates an output (into) vector with the statement by positional index for the empty backend. data points to a standard container compatible with SOCI vector bindings, described by exchange_type.
requirements: position must be a valid lvalue reference; the backend may read and/or increment it to reflect the next bind position.
data must be a non-null pointer to a compatible vector/container matching soci::details::exchange_type.
The container must remain valid for the duration of fetch operations.
Call during statement setup/binding phase before execution.

functions.name: soci::empty_vector_into_type_backend::pre_fetch
functions.description: Prepares the bound vector into buffer(s) prior to fetching rows. Typically used to resize/clear or set up internal state. Exact behavior for the empty backend is not documented.
requirements: Assumes a prior define_by_pos binding.
Called as part of the SOCI fetch lifecycle before retrieving rows.

functions.name: soci::empty_vector_into_type_backend::post_fetch
functions.description: Finalizes vector-result transfer after a fetch operation. gotData signals whether any rows were retrieved; ind may point to per-element indicators depending on backend. Empty-backend specifics are not documented.
requirements: If ind is provided, it must point to valid indicator storage matching the bound vector semantics expected by SOCI.
Must be called after pre_fetch/fetch cycle.
gotData should reflect whether data were produced.

functions.name: soci::empty_vector_into_type_backend::resize
functions.description: Requests the backend to resize the bound output vector to accommodate up to sz elements. Actual resizing behavior for the empty backend is not documented.
requirements: Caller provides the desired vector size as a non-negative size (std::size_t).
The underlying container referenced during bind must support resizing if the backend attempts it.

functions.name: soci::empty_vector_into_type_backend::size
functions.description: Returns the current size (number of elements) of the bound output vector as seen by the backend. Exact semantics for the empty backend are not documented.

functions.name: soci::empty_vector_into_type_backend::clean_up
functions.description: Releases any resources associated with the vector into binding for the empty backend.
requirements: Should be invoked when the binding is no longer needed (e.g., statement teardown or rebind).
After clean_up, do not use the instance for further fetches unless re-bound.

functions.name: soci::empty_standard_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos
functions.signature: void soci::empty_standard_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos(int& position, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type, bool readOnly)
functions.description: Binds a single input (use) value to the statement at a given position for the empty backend. data points to the value in application memory, described by exchange_type. readOnly indicates whether the value may be modified by the backend (typical SOCI semantics).
requirements: position must be a valid lvalue reference; the backend may read and/or increment it.
data must be a non-null pointer to storage matching soci::details::exchange_type.
The pointed-to data must remain valid until after execution completes.
readOnly should reflect caller intent; backend may rely on it.

functions.name: soci::empty_standard_use_type_backend::bind_by_name
functions.signature: void soci::empty_standard_use_type_backend::bind_by_name(const std::string& name, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type, bool readOnly)
functions.description: Binds a single input (use) value by parameter name for the empty backend. data points to application memory; name is the parameter identifier in the SQL text. readOnly indicates whether the value may be modified by the backend.
requirements: name must identify a valid parameter name expected by the prepared statement (naming rules are backend/SQL specific; unknown for empty backend).
data must be non-null and match soci::details::exchange_type.
The pointed-to data must remain valid until after execution completes.
readOnly should reflect caller intent.

functions.name: soci::empty_standard_use_type_backend::pre_use
functions.description: Prepares input (use) data before statement execution. ind, if provided, conveys null/defined state or other flags for the parameter(s). Empty-backend specifics are not documented.
requirements: If ind is non-null, it must point to valid indicator data corresponding to the bound value.
Should be called during statement execution workflow before sending data to the backend.

functions.name: soci::empty_standard_use_type_backend::post_use
functions.description: Called after statement execution to finalize use-bind processing. May update indicators or reflect output parameters. gotData indicates whether the execution produced any data (e.g., for returning parameters). Empty-backend specifics are not documented.
requirements: If ind is non-null, it must point to valid indicator storage for the bound parameter.
Called after execute; gotData should reflect whether data were produced for this binding.

functions.name: soci::empty_standard_use_type_backend::clean_up
functions.description: Releases any resources associated with the standard use binding for the empty backend.
requirements: Invoke when the binding is no longer needed or before re-binding.
Do not use the instance for further executions until re-bound after cleanup.

functions.name: soci::empty_vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos
functions.signature: void soci::empty_vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_pos(int& position, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type)
functions.description: Binds a vector of input (use) values to the statement by position for the empty backend. data points to a container compatible with SOCI vector bindings, described by exchange_type.
requirements: position must be a valid lvalue reference; backend may read and/or increment it.
data must be a non-null pointer to a compatible container matching the specified exchange type.

functions.name: soci::empty_vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_name
functions.signature: void soci::empty_vector_use_type_backend::bind_by_name(const std::string& name, void* data, soci::details::exchange_type type)
functions.description: Binds a vector of input (use) values by parameter name for the empty backend. data points to a compatible container; name identifies the SQL parameter.
requirements: name should match a parameter in the prepared statement (exact syntax unknown for empty backend).
data must be non-null and point to a compatible container for the given exchange type.
The container must remain valid until after execution completes.

functions.name: soci::empty_vector_use_type_backend::pre_use

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::empty_statement_backend
functions.description: Constructs an empty_statement_backend associated with the given empty_session_backend. This backend represents a statement object for the 'empty' SOCI backend.
requirements: session must be a valid, initialized soci::empty_session_backend that outlives the statement backend instance.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::alloc
functions.description: Allocates any resources necessary for the statement in the empty backend. Specific behavior is not documented.
requirements: Call before prepare/execute as required by SOCI core when initializing a statement.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::clean_up
functions.description: Releases resources associated with the statement in the empty backend.
requirements: Call when the statement is no longer needed.
Do not use the statement after cleanup unless re-initialized.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::prepare
functions.description: Prepares the given SQL query for execution in the empty backend with a specified statement type (e.g., one-time, repeatable). Exact semantics for the empty backend are not documented.
requirements: query should contain the SQL or command text to prepare.
eType must be a valid soci::details::statement_type value.
Must be called before execute/fetch.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::execute
functions.description: Executes the prepared statement, processing up to number rows depending on statement type. Returns an exec_fetch_result indicating outcome. Behavior for the empty backend is not documented.
requirements: number should be non-negative (typical SOCI convention for number of rows to process).
Statement should be prepared/bound as applicable before calling.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::fetch
functions.description: Fetches the next set of rows for the statement, up to number rows. Returns an exec_fetch_result indicating outcome. Behavior for the empty backend is not documented.
requirements: number should be non-negative.
Must be called after a successful execute on a fetch-capable statement.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::get_affected_rows
functions.description: Returns the number of rows affected by the last execute. Exact semantics for the empty backend are not documented.
requirements: Call after an execute that modifies rows (if supported).

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::get_number_of_rows
functions.description: Returns the number of rows in the current result set or last operation, as seen by the backend. Empty-backend specifics are not documented.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::get_parameter_name
functions.description: Returns the name of a parameter by index for the prepared statement. Indexing semantics are not documented for the empty backend.
requirements: index must refer to an existing parameter; indexing base (0- or 1-based) is unknown from this header.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::rewrite_for_procedure_call
functions.description: Returns a backend-specific rewrite of the supplied query suitable for procedure calls. For the empty backend, the transformation rules are not documented.
requirements: query should contain the procedure call text to be adapted.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::prepare_for_describe
functions.description: Prepares the statement so that its result set can be described (metadata inspection). Returns an integer status or column count depending on SOCI conventions. Empty-backend specifics are not documented.
requirements: Call before describe_column when describing results.

functions.name: soci::empty_statement_backend::describe_column
functions.signature: void soci::empty_statement_backend::describe_column(int colNum, soci::db_type& dbtype, std::string& columnName)
functions.description: Retrieves metadata for a result column: its db_type and optionally its name. colNum is the column index. Exact indexing base and behavior for the empty backend are not documented.
requirements: dbtype must be a valid reference that can be assigned to.
columnName must be a valid reference to receive the column name.
colNum must refer to a valid column (indexing base is not specified here).
Call after prepare_for_describe and, if required, after preparing/executing the statement.

functions.name: soci::empty_blob_backend::read_from_start
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::empty_blob_backend::read_from_start(void* buf, std::size_t toRead, std::size_t offset)
functions.description: Reads up to toRead bytes from the BLOB into buf, starting at byte offset from the beginning. Returns the number of bytes actually read. Behavior for the empty backend is not documented.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer to a buffer with capacity at least toRead bytes.
offset and toRead are sizes measured in bytes; offset is from the beginning of the BLOB.
The blob must be in a readable state and associated session must be valid.

functions.name: soci::empty_blob_backend::write_from_start
functions.signature: std::size_t soci::empty_blob_backend::write_from_start(const void* buf, std::size_t toWrite, std::size_t offset)

requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer to a buffer containing at least toWrite bytes of data.
offset and toWrite are sizes in bytes; offset is from the beginning of the BLOB.
The blob must be in a writable state and associated session must be valid.

functions.name: soci::empty_blob_backend::append

requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer to at least toWrite bytes of data.
The blob must be in a writable state and associated session must be valid.

functions.name: soci::empty_blob_backend::trim
functions.description: Truncates or extends the BLOB to exactly newLen bytes. Behavior for the empty backend is not documented.
requirements: newLen is the new desired BLOB size in bytes (std::size_t).
The blob must be in a writable state and associated session must be valid.

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: filesystem path string
# This generator produces a single bytes buffer that will be used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# in the provided fuzz stubs. We craft a compact corpus of plausible, valid path-like strings, including
# backend names and shared object hints, separated by null terminators so the harness can slice them.
# The stubs bound lengths (<96 etc.) and sanitize newlines/NULs; we avoid embedding NUL inside tokens
# and use ASCII-safe path characters.

_MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Safe characters for Unix/Windows-like paths and names (no NUL, no newline)
_SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._-"
_DIR_SEPS = ["/", "\\"]

_UNIX_EXTS = [".so", ".dylib", ""]
_WIN_EXTS = [".dll", ""]

# Common directories to make paths plausible
_UNIX_DIRS = ["/usr/lib", "/usr/local/lib", "/opt/lib", "/tmp", "/var/tmp", ".", "./build", "./out"]
_WIN_DIRS = [r"C:\\Windows\\System32", r"C:\\Program Files\\SOCI", r"C:\\Temp", r".\\build", r".\\out", "."]

# fopen modes used by the stub for reference when generating files
_MODES = ["r","rb","w","wb","a","ab","r+","rb+","w+","wb+","a+","ab+"]


def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure it doesn't start with a dot too often to vary behavior
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(_SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    if s[0] == '.':
        s = 'x' + s[1:]
    return s


def _rand_backend_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Backend names are typically short identifiers: e.g., "sqlite3", "postgresql", "oracle", "empty"
    candidates = [
        "sqlite3", "postgresql", "mysql", "oracle", "db2", "odbc", "empty",
        _rand_name(rng, 4, 10)
    ]
    name = rng.choice(candidates)
    # sanitize forbidden chars ':' will be sanitized by stub, but keep it valid already
    return name.replace(':', '_')


def _rand_so_basename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_name(rng, 5, 16)
    # Sometimes prefix with "libsoci_" like typical plugins
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = "libsoci_" + base
    return base


def _unix_so_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    d = rng.choice(_UNIX_DIRS)
    base = _rand_so_basename(rng)
    ext = rng.choice(_UNIX_EXTS)
    return f"{d}/{base}{ext}"


def _win_so_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    d = rng.choice(_WIN_DIRS)
    base = _rand_so_basename(rng)
    ext = rng.choice(_WIN_EXTS)
    # normalize slashes for Windows style
    return os.path.join(d, base + ext).replace('/', '\\')


def _path_segment(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    seg = _rand_name(rng, 1, 10)
    # Occasionally include a dot segment
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        seg = seg + "." + _rand_name(rng, 1, 5)
    return seg


def _rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of absolute/relative, Unix/Windows style
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Unix-like
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            # absolute
            start = "/"
        else:
            start = "./"
        depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
        parts = [_path_segment(rng) for _ in range(depth)]
        return start + "/".join(parts)
    else:
        # Windows-like
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            root = rng.choice(["C:", "D:", "E:"])
            start = root + "\\"
        else:
            start = ".\\"
        depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
        parts = [_path_segment(rng) for _ in range(depth)]
        return start + "\\".join(parts)


def _ensure_file(path: str, payload: bytes) -> None:
    # Best-effort create within current working dir only for relative paths to avoid touching system dirs.
    # The fuzz harness is expected to map FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to a file path it manages; we still try to
    # create plausible files if the chosen path is relative.
    try:
        if os.path.isabs(path):
            return
        d = os.path.dirname(path)
        if d and not os.path.exists(d):
            os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
        # Create small file
        with open(path, 'wb') as f:
            f.write(payload[:128])
    except Exception:
        pass


def _build_tokens(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tokens: List[str] = []

    # Paths for search_paths() mutation
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        tokens.append(_rand_path(rng))

    # Backend name candidates (non-empty, short)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        tokens.append(_rand_backend_name(rng))

    # Shared object path hints (mix platforms)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 7)):
        tokens.append(_unix_so_path(rng))
        tokens.append(_win_so_path(rng))

    # Filenames for soci::fopen
    # Create some actual small files for readable modes in relative paths
    for i in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        rel = os.path.join("fuzz_io", f"file_{i}_{_rand_name(rng,3,8)}.dat")
        tokens.append(rel)
        # Generate deterministic small payload
        payload = ("PAYLOAD_" + _rand_name(rng, 4, 12)).encode('ascii', 'ignore')
        _ensure_file(rel, payload)

    # Also include a few absolute-looking but likely non-existing paths
    tokens.append(_unix_so_path(rng))
    tokens.append(_win_so_path(rng))

    # Finally, generic short strings used widely
    tokens.extend([
        "",  # allow empty to exercise defaulting in stub where applicable
        "tmp",
        "plugins",
        "backends",
        "build/out",
        "C:\\Temp\\soci",
    ])

    # Deduplicate while preserving order, limit size
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[str] = []
    for t in tokens:
        if t not in seen:
            seen.add(t)
            # sanitize newlines and NULs defensively
            t = t.replace('\n', '_').replace('\x00', '_')
            uniq.append(t)
        if len(uniq) > 256:
            break

    return uniq


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    tokens = _build_tokens(rng)

    # For fopen, provide one mode string explicitly to increase chance of valid IO
    mode = rng.choice(_MODES)
    tokens.append(mode)

    # Join tokens with NUL separators; FUZZ harness typically consumes sequentially.
    # Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes.
    encoded_parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    for t in tokens:
        b = t.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
        if len(b) > 256:
            b = b[:256]
        # account for separator
        need = len(b) + 1
        if total + need > _MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        encoded_parts.append(b)
        encoded_parts.append(b"\x00")
        total += need

    return b"".join(encoded_parts)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: identifier string
# - Short, human-readable key/name used as identifiers: backend names, option names, etc.
# - Should avoid whitespace/control chars and separators like '=' ':' '\n' '\0'.
# - Common allowed chars: A-Z a-z 0-9 underscore, dash. First char typically letter or underscore.
# - Fuzzer stubs often truncate to certain lengths (e.g., 16, 24, 32). We'll generate within these bounds.
# - The harness packs a single buffer and will reuse it across FUZZ_PARAM_STR sites. We therefore
#   compose the buffer as multiple newline-separated candidate identifiers so each call can slice
#   a distinct piece while the stub replaces newlines. But stubs explicitly sanitize newlines to '_'.
#   To keep inputs straightforward and valid before sanitization, we avoid newlines and instead
#   provide multiple identifiers separated by spaces is risky (spaces are stripped). So we provide
#   a single identifier per buffer to be robust.
#
# Strategy
# - Generate a single identifier likely to exercise code paths:
#   * Vary length among {1..32} with bias to common caps like 8, 16, 24, 32.
#   * Start with letter or underscore.
#   * Include mix of letters, digits, underscores, and dashes.
# - To also help paths expecting path-like strings (shared object hint) but still valid identifier,
#   we sometimes include dashes and underscores sequences.
# - The output is bytes, ASCII only, <=4096 bytes (we keep it short).

ALPHA = string.ascii_letters + "_"
ALNUM_USCORE_DASH = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"


def _biased_length(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias towards common truncation thresholds
    choices = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32]
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        return rng.choice(choices)
    return rng.randint(1, 32)


def _make_identifier(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    length = max(min_len, min(_biased_length(rng), max_len))
    first = rng.choice(ALPHA)
    # Occasionally start with underscore to test that branch
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        first = "_"
    rest_chars: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(length - 1):
        ch = rng.choice(ALNUM_USCORE_DASH)
        # Avoid consecutive dashes sometimes to keep it cleaner
        if rest_chars and rest_chars[-1] == '-' and ch == '-':
            ch = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_")
        rest_chars.append(ch)
    ident = first + ("".join(rest_chars))
    # Ensure it's not empty or just dashes/underscores
    if all(c in "-_" for c in ident):
        ident = ident + "a"
    return ident


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    ident = _make_identifier(rng)
    # Some stubs sanitize ':' '\n' '\0' and spaces; we ensure none are present.
    # Also ensure length limits; many stubs cap at 16/24/32. Keep <= 32.
    ident = ident[:32]
    # As a final fallback, provide a default if anything went wrong
    if not ident:
        ident = "id"
    return ident.encode("ascii")

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# Target format: arbitrary byte string
# Goal: Provide interesting yet valid buffers for many different code paths:
# - Printable SQL-like snippets
# - Name=value option strings
# - UTF-8 that is valid and invalid
# - Small and large sizes (bounded <= 4096)
# - Binary blobs with zero bytes
# - Paths/filenames
# The fuzzer stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME; both expect
# a bytes buffer they can slice from to produce strings and other data.
# We'll emit a container that concatenates multiple segments separated by
# distinct markers to increase variety on first consumption.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rnd(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return r.randbytes(n) if hasattr(r, 'randbytes') else bytes([r.randrange(256) for _ in range(n)])

def _gen_sql(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose a short SQL-like statement with parameters and keywords
    cols = ["id", "name", "value", "created_at", "data"]
    tbls = ["t", "items", "logs", "users", "metrics"]
    kw = ["SELECT", "INSERT", "UPDATE", "DELETE"]
    op = r.choice(kw)
    if op == "SELECT":
        csel = ", ".join(r.sample(cols, k=r.randint(1, min(3, len(cols)))))
        where = r.choice(["", f" WHERE {r.choice(cols)} = :p{r.randint(1,9)}"]) \
                + r.choice(["", f" AND {r.choice(cols)} > ?"]) \
                + r.choice(["", f" ORDER BY {r.choice(cols)} DESC"]) \
                + r.choice(["", " LIMIT 10"]) \
                + r.choice(["", " OFFSET 5"]) \
                + ";"
        return f"{op} {csel} FROM {r.choice(tbls)}{where}".encode('utf-8')
    elif op == "INSERT":
        k = r.randint(1, 3)
        use = r.sample(cols, k=k)
        vals = ", ".join([":"+c for c in use])
        return f"INSERT INTO {r.choice(tbls)} ({', '.join(use)}) VALUES ({vals});".encode()
    elif op == "UPDATE":
        setc = r.choice(cols)
        return f"UPDATE {r.choice(tbls)} SET {setc} = :{setc} WHERE id = :id;".encode()
    else:
        return f"DELETE FROM {r.choice(tbls)} WHERE id = :id;".encode()

def _gen_options_kv(r: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    # space-separated name=value pairs; sanitize names to avoid spaces/equals
    def mkname():
        base = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters+string.digits+"_-") for _ in range(r.randint(2, 10)))
        return base
    def mkval():
        # values may contain quotes and spaces; quote sometimes
        raw = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters+string.digits+" _-:/.,@") for _ in range(r.randint(0, 20)))
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            q = r.choice(['"', "'"])
            return q + raw + q
        return raw
    pairs = [f"{mkname()}={mkval()}" for _ in range(count)]
    return (' '.join(pairs)).encode('utf-8')

def _gen_utf8(r: random.Random, valid_ratio=0.6, max_len=256) -> bytes:
    # Mix valid UTF-8 with some invalid sequences
    buf = bytearray()
    target = r.randint(0, max_len)
    while len(buf) < target:
        roll = r.random()
        if roll < valid_ratio:
            # append a valid codepoint (1-4 bytes)
            cp_choice = r.random()
            if cp_choice < 0.7:
                buf.append(r.randrange(0x20, 0x7f))
            else:
                # pick a broader range excluding surrogates
                cp = r.randrange(0, 0x10FFFF)
                if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                    cp = 0x20
                s = chr(cp).encode('utf-8', 'strict')
                buf.extend(s)
        else:
            # invalid: random leading continuation or truncated multibyte
            t = r.randrange(3)
            if t == 0:
                buf.append(r.randrange(0x80, 0xC0))
            elif t == 1:
                buf.append(r.randrange(0xC0, 0xE0))  # lead without continuation
            else:
                buf.extend(_rnd(r, r.randint(1, 3)))
    return bytes(buf[:max_len])

def _gen_filename(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # plausible filename with directories
    parts = []
    depth = r.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        name = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters+string.digits+"_-.") for _ in range(r.randint(1, 8)))
        parts.append(name)
    leaf = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters+string.digits+"_-.") for _ in range(r.randint(1, 12)))
    path = "/".join(parts + [leaf]) if parts else leaf
    # sometimes tmp dir style
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        path = "/tmp/" + path
    return path.encode('utf-8')

def _gen_numbers(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # mixture of little-endian integers and doubles to feed numeric consumers
    data = bytearray()
    count = r.randint(2, 8)
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = r.randrange(4)
        if choice == 0:
            data.extend(struct.pack('<i', r.randrange(-2**31, 2**31)))
        elif choice == 1:
            data.extend(struct.pack('<I', r.randrange(0, 2**32)))
        elif choice == 2:
            # double
            data.extend(struct.pack('<d', r.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)))
        else:
            data.extend(struct.pack('<q', r.randrange(-2**63+1, 2**63-1)))
    return bytes(data)

def _gen_blob(r: random.Random, max_len=1024) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(0, max_len)
    # include zero bytes at random intervals
    blob = bytearray(_rnd(r, n))
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, max(1, n//16))):
        if not blob:
            break
        blob[r.randrange(len(blob))] = 0
    return bytes(blob)

def _segment(tag: str, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Segment with a simple header: b"--TAG--\n" + len + data
    hdr = f"--{tag}--\n".encode('ascii')
    ln = struct.pack('<I', len(payload))
    return hdr + ln + payload

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    segments: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) SQL-like
    segments.append(_segment('SQL', _gen_sql(r)))

    # 2) Options string
    segments.append(_segment('OPTS', _gen_options_kv(r, r.randint(1, 5))))

    # 3) Valid/invalid UTF-8 mixture
    segments.append(_segment('UTF8', _gen_utf8(r, valid_ratio=0.6, max_len=512)))

    # 4) Filename
    segments.append(_segment('FILE', _gen_filename(r)))

    # 5) Numbers (binary)
    segments.append(_segment('NUM', _gen_numbers(r)))

    # 6) Binary blob with zeros
    segments.append(_segment('BLOB', _gen_blob(r, max_len=1024)))

    # 7) Short strings for parameter names/values
    short_pairs = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        name = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters+string.digits+"_-") for _ in range(r.randint(1, 12)))
        val = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters+string.digits+" _-:/.,@") for _ in range(r.randint(0, 24)))
        short_pairs.append(f"{name}\t{val}")
    segments.append(_segment('PAIR', ('\n'.join(short_pairs)).encode('utf-8')))

    # 8) Mixed lengths: tiny and medium strings
    tiny = bytes([r.randrange(32, 127) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 8))])
    med = bytes([r.randrange(32, 127) for _ in range(r.randint(32, 256))])
    segments.append(_segment('TINY', tiny))
    segments.append(_segment('MED', med))

    # 9) Additional UTF sequences for converters
    segments.append(_segment('UTF8V', _gen_utf8(r, valid_ratio=0.9, max_len=256)))

    out = b''.join(segments)
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return out

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets stubs that construct soci::values for column_info conversion.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used for column names and also sometimes for DATA_TYPE in optional<T> path.
# FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) and FUZZ_PARAM(uint32_t) are consumed to pick among data types and numeric attributes.
# We return a bytes buffer that encodes a sequence of tokens that the harness will read in order.
# While we don't know the exact FUZZ framework wire format, a common pattern is to provide a stream
# of bytes from which different functions consume variable-sized chunks. To maximize validity,
# we produce a structured sequence of ASCII strings and little-endian integers in a predictable order.
#
# Layout we emit (all little-endian for integers):
# - A set of records; each record can satisfy both stubs when read linearly.
# - For each record:
#   * Column name string (length byte N, followed by N bytes UTF-8)
#   * 4-byte unsigned int: type_choice (0..9) to drive switch in first stub
#   * 4-byte uint32: CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH
#   * 4-byte uint32: NUMERIC_PRECISION (<=1023)
#   * 4-byte uint32: NUMERIC_SCALE (<=63)
#   * 4-byte unsigned int: flag influencing numeric scale bump
#   * 4-byte unsigned int: is_yes flag for IS_NULLABLE
#   * Optional<T> path extras:
#       - Column name string #2 (can differ; length+bytes)
#       - 4-byte unsigned int mode (0..2) controlling null vs non-null
#       - 4-byte unsigned int for selecting DATA_TYPE from a small array
#       - 4-byte uint32: charMaxLen
#       - 4-byte uint32: numPrecision (<=18)
#       - 4-byte uint32: numScale (<=5)
#       - 4-byte unsigned int to pick YES/NO for IS_NULLABLE
#
# Strings are chosen from reasonable sets and trimmed to <= 64 chars.
# We repeat multiple records to give the fuzzer ample initial data.

SQL_TYPES = [
    "text", "INTEGER", "bigint", "double precision", "numeric",
    "timestamp", "blob", "oid", "xml", "varchar"
]

OPT_TYPES = [
    "TEXT", "INTEGER", "BIGINT", "DOUBLE", "NUMERIC", "DATE", "BLOB", "XML", "VARCHAR"
]

COLNAME_TOKENS = [
    "id", "name", "description", "created_at", "updated_at", "price", "amount",
    "count", "flag", "payload", "xml_data", "blob_data", "value", "col", "Status",
    "USER", "OrderID", "äöü", "长列名", "very_long_column_name_exercising_paths"
]

YESNO = ["YES", "NO"]


def _pack_str(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 64:
        b = b[:64]
    # length as 1 byte capped at 255
    lb = len(b)
    if lb > 255:
        b = b[:255]
        lb = 255
    return struct.pack('B', lb) + b


def _u32(n: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', n & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _pick_dtype_by_choice(choice: int) -> str:
    return SQL_TYPES[choice % len(SQL_TYPES)]


def _make_record(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()

    # Column name 1
    col = rng.choice(COLNAME_TOKENS)
    # Occasionally add suffix/prefix to vary
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        col = (rng.choice(["", "tbl_", "col_"]) + col + rng.choice(["", "_idx", "_col"]))
    out += _pack_str(col)

    # type_choice driving switch
    type_choice = rng.randrange(0, 10)
    out += _u32(type_choice)

    # CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH
    char_len = rng.randrange(0, 4096)
    out += _u32(char_len)

    # NUMERIC_PRECISION (<=1023), NUMERIC_SCALE (<=63)
    precision = rng.randrange(0, 1024)
    scale = rng.randrange(0, 64)
    out += _u32(precision)
    out += _u32(scale)

    # scale bump flag
    out += _u32(rng.getrandbits(32))

    # IS_NULLABLE flag
    out += _u32(rng.getrandbits(32))

    # Optional<T> stub specific inputs
    col2 = col if rng.random() < 0.5 else rng.choice(COLNAME_TOKENS)
    out += _pack_str(col2)

    mode = rng.randrange(0, 3)  # 0=null, 1/2 non-null
    out += _u32(mode)

    dtype_sel = rng.randrange(0, len(OPT_TYPES))
    out += _u32(dtype_sel)

    out += _u32(rng.randrange(0, 2048))           # charMaxLen
    out += _u32(rng.randrange(0, 19))             # numPrecision
    out += _u32(rng.randrange(0, 6))              # numScale
    out += _u32(rng.getrandbits(32))              # YES/NO picker

    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build between 3 and 12 records; cap total size to 4096 bytes
    nrecs = rng.randrange(5, 10)
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    for _ in range(nrecs):
        rec = _make_record(rng)
        chunks.append(rec)
        if sum(len(c) for c in chunks) > 3800:
            break

    buf = b"".join(chunks)

    # Prepend a small header with a magic and count to help frameworks that parse structured blobs.
    header = b"SCOL" + _u32(len(chunks))
    out = header + buf

    # Ensure under 4096
    return out[:4096]

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets SOCI metadata-related fuzzers that expect to read bytes
# and interpret them as strings/integers for constructing soci::values fields
# such as COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE, CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH, NUMERIC_PRECISION,
# NUMERIC_SCALE, and IS_NULLABLE.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a compact, self-describing binary blob containing a random, but valid,
#   set of fields that the fuzzer harness will likely pull from FUZZ_PARAM_STR and
#   FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) calls.
# - Include multiple candidate strings up front so FUZZ_PARAM_STR() draws from
#   meaningful tokens exercising different branches in type_conversion<column_info>::from_base().
# - Provide a series of 32-bit integers covering numeric fields within reasonable
#   bounds expected by the code paths.
# - Ensure presence of YES/NO strings for IS_NULLABLE.
# - Keep the buffer size small (< 4096 bytes).
#
# Buffer layout (little endian lengths):
# [u16 N_str]
#   repeat N_str times: [u16 len][bytes string]
# [u16 N_u32]
#   repeat N_u32 times: [u32 value]
# [u16 N_yesno]
#   repeat N_yesno times: [1 byte: 0=>"YES", 1=>"NO"]
#
# The fuzzer typically interleaves FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int), so
# we place a variety of strings first (column names and data types), then a pool of
# integers for sizes/precision/scale and mode selectors, and finally a few YES/NO flags
# that can be consumed as strings (some fuzzers store them as string fields).

DATA_TYPES = [
    "text", "TEXT",
    "INTEGER", "int", "INT",
    "bigint", "BIGINT",
    "double precision", "DOUBLE",
    "numeric", "NUMBER", "NUMERIC",
    "timestamp", "date", "DATE", "time", "TIME",
    "blob", "BLOB", "oid", "OID",
    "xml", "XML",
    "varchar", "VARCHAR", "char", "CHAR",
]

# Column name seeds to mix with random strings
COLNAME_SEEDS = [
    "col", "id", "user_name", "amount", "created_at", "description",
    "Üñîçødê",  # unicode edge
    "",  # allow empty, harness may replace with default "col"
]


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_"
    return "".join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _build_strings(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    strings: List[bytes] = []

    # Column names: mix seeds and random
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        base = r.choice(COLNAME_SEEDS)
        if base == "":
            s = base
        else:
            # sometimes append a suffix for variability
            if r.random() < 0.6:
                s = f"{base}_{_rand_ascii(r, 1, 6)}"
            else:
                s = base
        # limit to 64 like the optional fuzzer
        if len(s) > 64:
            s = s[:64]
        strings.append(s.encode('utf-8'))

    # Data types: provide a curated set covering branches
    picked = r.sample(DATA_TYPES, k=min(len(DATA_TYPES), r.randint(8, 16)))
    for dt in picked:
        strings.append(dt.encode('utf-8'))

    # Also provide YES/NO as strings directly for IS_NULLABLE when taken from FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    strings.append(b"YES")
    strings.append(b"NO")

    # Add some generic varchar-like tokens to drive string family
    for w in ["varchar(255)", "VarChar", "CHAR(10)"]:
        strings.append(w.encode('utf-8'))

    # Ensure there are at least a dozen strings
    while len(strings) < 16:
        strings.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 8).encode('utf-8'))

    return strings


def _build_u32s(r: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    vals: List[int] = []
    # Typical bounds used in stubs
    # char_len up to a few KB
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        vals.append(r.randint(0, 4096))
    # precision small
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        vals.append(r.randint(0, 1024))
    # scale small
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        vals.append(r.randint(0, 64))
    # mode/type selectors
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        vals.append(r.getrandbits(32))
    return vals


def _pack_strings(strings: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # u16 count, then each as u16 len + data (truncated to 512 to stay small)
    out = bytearray()
    count = min(len(strings), 200)
    out += struct.pack('<H', count)
    for s in strings[:count]:
        s2 = s[:512]
        out += struct.pack('<H', len(s2))
        out += s2
    return bytes(out)


def _pack_u32s(vals: List[int]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    count = min(len(vals), 512)
    out += struct.pack('<H', count)
    for v in vals[:count]:
        out += struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    return bytes(out)


def _pack_yesno(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Provide a small pool of YES/NO flags encoded as 1 byte selector (0=>YES,1=>NO)
    out = bytearray()
    out += struct.pack('<H', n)
    for _ in range(n):
        out += struct.pack('<B', 0 if r.random() < 0.5 else 1)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    strings = _build_strings(r)
    u32s = _build_u32s(r)
    yesno_count = r.randint(2, 8)

    blob = bytearray()
    blob += _pack_strings(strings)
    blob += _pack_u32s(u32s)
    blob += _pack_yesno(r, yesno_count)

    # Ensure maximum size limit
    return bytes(blob[:4096])

import random
import struct
import itertools

# This generator targets SOCI column metadata construction in the fuzz stubs.
# The stubs request strings and integral values via FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int/uint32_t).
# We provide a compact, seeded byte stream encoding a sequence of such parameters in the
# order that will produce valid, interesting inputs for both stubs.
#
# Encoding format:
#  - Magic header: b"SCOL\x00\x01" to help desync recovery (optional for the harness but keeps inputs recognizable).
#  - Then we emit a sequence of logical fields likely to be consumed by the stubs in order:
#    For soci::type_conversion<soci::column_info>::from_base stub:
#      1) Column name (string)
#      2) type_choice (unsigned int)
#      3) char_len (uint32)
#      4) precision (uint32)
#      5) scale (uint32)
#      6) extra unsigned controlling numeric scale bump
#      7) is_yes toggle unsigned
#    For soci::type_conversion<std::optional<T>>::from_base stub:
#      8) mode (unsigned int 0..2) controls indicator i_null vs i_ok
#      9) colName (string)
#     10) unsigned driving charMaxLen
#     11) unsigned driving numPrecision
#     12) unsigned driving numScale
#     13) unsigned driving isNullable YES/NO
#     14) trailing filler strings to feed any extra FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers gracefully
#
# String encoding: [u16 length][bytes], ASCII with occasional keyword tokens
# Integers: little-endian 32-bit unsigned
#
# We deliberately choose values to exercise different DATA_TYPE branches and numeric cases while
# remaining valid. Sizes capped well below 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Bias towards alnum and underscore
    alphabet = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_'
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _enc_str(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 65535:
        b = b[:65535]
    return struct.pack('<H', len(b)) + b

# Data type options mirrored from the stub switch and optional harness array
_DT_SWITCH = [
    'text', 'INTEGER', 'bigint', 'double precision', 'numeric',
    'timestamp', 'blob', 'oid', 'xml', 'varchar'
]
# For the second stub, it rotates over this array via mode
_DT_ROTATE = ['TEXT', 'INTEGER', 'BIGINT', 'DOUBLE', 'NUMERIC', 'DATE', 'BLOB', 'XML', 'VARCHAR']

# Produce one coherent buffer covering both stubs expectations

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = bytearray()
    out += b'SCOL\x00\x01'

    # 1) Column name for first stub
    # Prefer a realistic identifier with mixed cases
    base_name = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12)
    # Occasionally pick common column names to help equality/assertions
    common = ['id', 'name', 'amount', 'created_at', 'payload', 'col']
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        base_name = rng.choice(common)
    out += _enc_str(base_name)

    # 2) type_choice for the first stub switch (0..9)
    # Cycle through data types by seed while adding variance
    type_choice = rng.randrange(10)
    out += _u32(type_choice)

    # 3) char_len (uint32) — keep small/moderate
    char_len = rng.randint(0, 4096)
    out += _u32(char_len)

    # 4) precision (0..1023) as per stub modulo 1024
    precision = rng.randint(0, 1023)
    out += _u32(precision)

    # 5) scale (0..63) as per stub modulo 64, prefer some non-zero values
    scale = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 10, 15, 31, 63])
    out += _u32(scale)

    # 6) extra unsigned to sometimes force non-zero scale when dtype is numeric/number
    bump_flag = 1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0
    out += _u32(bump_flag)

    # 7) is_yes toggle: 0/1 for YES/NO selection
    is_yes = 1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0
    out += _u32(is_yes)

    # 8) mode for optional<T> stub: 0=null, 1/2=non-null with varying dtype selection
    mode = rng.randrange(3)
    out += _u32(mode)

    # 9) Column name for second stub
    second_name = base_name
    # Occasionally vary name to cover both same and different-name scenarios
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        second_name = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 16)
    out += _enc_str(second_name)

    # 10) unsigned for charMaxLen (kept under 1024 by stub modulo)
    out += _u32(rng.randint(0, 5000))

    # 11) unsigned for numPrecision (stub modulo 19)
    out += _u32(rng.randint(0, 100))

    # 12) unsigned for numScale (stub modulo 6)
    out += _u32(rng.randint(0, 50))

    # 13) unsigned for isNullable: bit 0 checked by stub
    out += _u32(rng.getrandbits(32))

    # 14) Extra strings to satisfy any additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls gracefully.
    # Include tokens that exercise type name pattern matching in type_conversion<column_info>::from_base
    extra_tokens = [
        'VARCHAR(255)', 'CHAR', 'NUMBER', 'NUMERIC(10,2)', 'DATE', 'TIME', 'TIMESTAMP',
        'CLOB', 'BLOB', 'XMLTYPE', 'oid', 'text', 'char varying', 'DOUBLE', 'integer'
    ]
    # Emit a small, bounded number of extras
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        token = rng.choice(extra_tokens)
        # Sometimes random text
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            token = _rand_ascii(rng, 4, 20)
        piece = _enc_str(token)
        if len(out) + len(piece) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += piece

    # Ensure we don't exceed size limit
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: connection string
# Used by:
# - soci::connection_parameters::connection_parameters (then set_connect_string)
# - soci::connection_parameters::set_connect_string
# - soci::session::open (backend "empty", arbitrary connect string)
# - soci::backend_factory::make_session (constructs connection_parameters from a full connect string)
#
# Valid inputs:
# - Free-form strings
# - Space-separated name=value pairs, with optional quoted values (single or double quotes)
# - URIs like "empty://..." are also accepted by constructor taking a full connect string.
#
# Strategy:
# Generate a variety of realistic connection strings that exercise:
# - Empty/very short strings
# - Plain text
# - Space-separated options with different value types (ints, bools, empty, quoted, escaped, unicode)
# - Duplicate keys, unknown keys
# - URI-style forms (backend://name?opt=val;opt2=val2 or backend name followed by options)
# - Strings containing whitespace, tabs, newlines (within quotes) to exercise parser robustness
# - Reasonable length limits (<= 1024 in stub, and global limit 4096)
#
# The function returns bytes, as required by the fuzzer harness FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# to seed initial buffers.

MAX_SIZE = 1024

BOOL_TRUE = ["1", "yes", "true", "on", ""]
BOOL_FALSE = ["0", "no", "false", "off"]

BACKENDS = [
    "empty",  # definitely present in target
    "sqlite3", "postgresql", "mysql", "oracle", "odbc"
]

OPT_KEYS_COMMON = [
    "host", "port", "user", "password", "dbname", "service", "schema",
    "sslmode", "charset", "timeout", "application_name", "search_path",
    "readOnly", "autocommit", "keepalive", "connect_timeout", "encoding"
]

# Include options that are likely ignored to exercise unknown-option paths
OPT_KEYS_EXTRA = [
    "x", "y", "z", "flag", "empty", "UPPER", "MiXeD", "retries", "debug",
    "on_error", "pool_size", "quote_test"
]

QUOTES = ['"', "'"]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "Δ", "é", "漢字", "🙂", "ß", "ø", "¡", "¿", "тест", "árvíztűrő tükörfúrógép"
]

ESCAPABLE = [" ", "\t", "\n", "\\", "=", ":", ";"]


def rnd_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(seq)


def gen_simple_freeform(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Plain free-form string, possibly empty or short
    length = rng.randint(0, 64)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:.@/\t"
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))


def maybe_quote(rng: random.Random, val: str) -> str:
    # Quote with single or double quotes, sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        q = rnd_choice(rng, QUOTES)
        # Occasionally include the quote inside by escaping
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            esc = "\\" if q == '"' else "\\"
            val = val.replace(q, esc + q)
        return f"{q}{val}{q}"
    return val


def gen_value(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    t = rng.random()
    if t < 0.2:
        return rnd_choice(rng, BOOL_TRUE + BOOL_FALSE)
    elif t < 0.35:
        return str(rng.randint(-10_000, 100_000))
    elif t < 0.5:
        # Unicode-rich value
        base = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            base += ":" + str(rng.randint(1, 9999))
        return maybe_quote(rng, base)
    elif t < 0.7:
        # Include escapable characters
        segs = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
            segs.append(seg)
        # insert random escapable separator
        glue = rnd_choice(rng, ESCAPABLE)
        return maybe_quote(rng, glue.join(segs))
    elif t < 0.85:
        # Empty value (still valid in parser)
        return maybe_quote(rng, "")
    else:
        # Typical hostname or path
        host = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)))
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            return f"{host}.local"
        path_parts = [host] + [
            ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)))
            for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))
        ]
        return "/" + "/".join(path_parts)


def gen_kv_pair(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    key_pool = OPT_KEYS_COMMON + OPT_KEYS_EXTRA
    key = rnd_choice(rng, key_pool)
    val = gen_value(rng)
    # Sometimes add spaces around '='
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        return f"{key} = {val}"
    return f"{key}={val}"


def gen_space_separated_options(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(1, 10)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(n):
        parts.append(gen_kv_pair(rng))
    # Occasionally duplicate a key to test overwriting
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(gen_kv_pair(rng))
    s = " ".join(parts)
    # Occasionally introduce tabs/newlines between options
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        s = s.replace(" ", rnd_choice(rng, ["\t", "\n"]))
    return s


def gen_uri_form(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    backend = rnd_choice(rng, BACKENDS)
    # authority or db name
    authority = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)))
    base = f"{backend}://{authority}"
    # Build query-like parameters using ; or & or space-separated after ?
    params = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)):
        k = rnd_choice(rng, OPT_KEYS_COMMON + OPT_KEYS_EXTRA)
        v = gen_value(rng)
        # For URI, avoid raw spaces; percent-encode some characters, or quote
        v_str = str(v)
        if v_str and any(ch in v_str for ch in " \t\n;=&?"):
            # naive percent-encoding of spaces and semicolons
            v_str = v_str.replace(" ", "%20").replace(";", "%3B").replace("\n", "%0A").replace("\t", "%09")
        params.append(f"{k}={v_str}")
    sep = rnd_choice(rng, ["&", ";"])  # both common separators
    query = sep.join(params)
    return f"{base}?{query}"


def gen_backend_name_plus_options(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Form: "backendName key=value key2=\"val\" ..."
    backend = rnd_choice(rng, BACKENDS)
    opts = gen_space_separated_options(rng)
    return f"{backend} {opts}"


def gen_empty_backend_minimal(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Minimal but valid for empty backend: "empty" or "empty://"
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return "empty"
    return "empty://" + gen_simple_freeform(rng)


def assemble_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands = []
    cands.append(gen_simple_freeform(rng))
    cands.append(gen_space_separated_options(rng))
    cands.append(gen_uri_form(rng))
    cands.append(gen_backend_name_plus_options(rng))
    cands.append(gen_empty_backend_minimal(rng))
    # Edge-case variants
    cands.append("")  # empty
    cands.append(" ")  # single space
    # Quoted-only value
    cands.append("password=\"\" user='u s e r' dbname=tes\tdb")
    # Boolean focus
    cands.append("autocommit=on readOnly=off timeout=0")
    # Duplicates and mixed case
    cands.append("HOST=LocalHost host=example.com PORT=5432 port=15432")
    return cands


def choose_and_trim(rng: random.Random, cands: List[str]) -> str:
    s = rng.choice(cands)
    # Occasionally concatenate multiple forms to reach parser branches
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        extra = rng.choice(cands)
        # Join with space to keep a single connect string
        s = (s + " " + extra).strip()
    if len(s) > MAX_SIZE:
        s = s[:MAX_SIZE]
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    candidates = assemble_candidates(rng)
    s = choose_and_trim(rng, candidates)
    # Ensure final size constraint (global <= 4096 already satisfied by MAX_SIZE)
    data = s.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string

# This generator produces bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used as option name in
# soci::connection_parameters::is_option_on fuzzer. The stub sanitizes the
# name by replacing NUL/space/newline/CR/'=' with 'b' and truncates to 16.
# It then sets the option to either a true token ("on") or false token ("no").
# Our goal is to generate interesting, yet valid names that exercise parsing
# paths: empty (becomes "bool"), varying lengths, mixed chars including ones
# that get replaced, with/without '=' and whitespace, unicode-ish bytes, etc.

TRUE_TOKENS = [b"", b"1", b"yes", b"true", b"on"]
FALSE_TOKENS = [b"0", b"no", b"false", b"off"]

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-:."
REPLACED_CHARS = [0x00, ord(' '), ord('\n'), ord('\r'), ord('=')]

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _make_name_variants(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a list of candidate names to choose from; some include chars
    # that will be replaced by the stub, others are clean.
    variants = []

    # 1) Empty -> fuzzer replaces with "bool"
    variants.append(b"")

    # 2) Simple short names
    variants.extend([b"flag", b"opt", b"x", b"y", b"feature", b"debug"])

    # 3) Max length (16) clean ascii
    variants.append(bytes('A'*16, 'ascii'))

    # 4) Names with spaces/newlines/CR/'=' that will be sanitized to 'b'
    variants.extend([
        b"has space",            # space -> 'b'
        b"line\nend",            # \n -> 'b'
        b"car\rret",             # \r -> 'b'
        b"eq=sign",               # '=' -> 'b'
        b"mix = \n \r\0",       # includes all replaceds (NUL included)
    ])

    # 5) Non-ASCII bytes that remain as-is (except if they match replaced set)
    variants.append(bytes([0xC2, 0xA9, 0xE2, 0x98, 0x83]))  # UTF-8 ©☃ bytes

    # 6) Random length 1..24 (will be truncated to 16 in stub), with mixed chars
    for _ in range(5):
        L = rng.randint(1, 24)
        b = bytearray()
        for _ in range(L):
            choice = rng.random()
            if choice < 0.6:
                b.append(ord(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII)))
            elif choice < 0.85:
                b.append(rng.choice(REPLACED_CHARS))
            else:
                b.append(rng.randrange(0, 256))
        variants.append(bytes(b))

    return rng.choice(variants)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide whether to emit a true token buffer or a false token buffer.
    # Although the stub chooses val internally, our buffer only supplies the
    # name. Still, we randomize to diversify names but the content is just one
    # buffer: the name string input consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR.

    name = _make_name_variants(rng)

    # Ensure the total buffer is within 4096 bytes; our names are tiny.
    # Return the name bytes directly; fuzzer will use it for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
    return name
